body: I went with my wife and daughter and her husband ( A British subject) recently. The experience was horrible ! The tour guide was obnoxious and very disrespectful. I was originally a Sri Lankan and now a New Zealander and the guide completely avoided toking to me and my wife and was smiling only with people with a white skin! I anyway made no comments and said thank you to him at the end! He looked very surprised and didn’t utter a word back! The culture of sucking up to the white man and being disrespectful towards brown skin is typical of colonial times and it is time we give up this behaviour!!Products were terribly overpriced and the whole estate is run down and lot of foreigners who were there walked away disgusted !!
title: Handungoda tea estate - Do not go there !!

body: While their tea is fantastic I wasn’t amazed about the labor conditions. Tourist shop is nice and cold, factory is like 40 degrees
title: Bitter sweet

body: A fascinating experience worth a couple of hours of anyone’s time if they are in the south of Sri Lanka. You will learn how tea makes it from plant to cup in the company of a very enthusiastic and knowledgeable guide such a the incomparable Bandula who had a detailed answer to any question that I posed him. Set in a beautiful location, the tour will also appeal to those who enjoy tropical gardens and anyone who wants to see the impressive vintage machines that the Herman company still use in their tea making process.
title: Something for everyone’s taste.

body: A nice guided tour to see how a tea garden looks and how it works from bush to ready cup of tea. Didn’t think that any of the varieties you could taste in the end was something that directly appealed to me but bought cheaper and tastier teas elsewhere instead.
title: Nice little ride.

body: Interesting tour round a small tea plantation and factory. Halfway round they serve chocolate cake and tea on the terrace which was lovely. Tea tasting at the end is set up like wine tasting and there’s lots of variety. Great way to spend a morning
title: Lovely tour

body: We drove 30 min. to the estate from Weligama and were lucky to join a group that just started the journey with Mr Dudley on the estate. We've got a thorough explanation of the tea growing business starting from propagation to harvest and onto the processing. Saw the picking ladies, got a nice cup of the signature blend of the estate, checked out the machinery, and than we had an extensive tea tasting experience. This trip worth every second! Special thanks to Mr Dudley for his expertise and everyone on the estate to show us the details of this business! Highly recommend!
title: High quality experience for half a day program

body: What a delightful experience !We arrived and were greeted by a member of staff who oozed years of experience. Toured the tea estate and learnt about how they manage the tea bushes, how they are plucked and the various types of tea from the same bush. Tea factory was fascinating and then teas tasting. All in all very interesting and good value. Loved the tipping box at the end as the guides refused tips!
title: What a delightful experience

body: Very informative tour of the tea plantation and the factory area. Break with cake and tea, as well as a tea tasting at the end!
title: From tea leaf to cup

body: A Well organised and informative tour. Tea and cake in the tour price, plus another 40 teas to taste. No hard sell either. Very good tour
title: Tea plantation tour

body: The plantation tour was fantastic, definitely up my ally as I love tea and enjoy being outside with nature. We were a small group of 4 which was nice as the tour felt more personal. Our guide was very informative and learnt I a lot from him about the tea picking process. He answered all of our questions and you can tell he is passionate about tea. The tour lasts for a hour and the walk around the estate wasn't strainous, inside the tea factory you got to see how the tea is made along with seeing machinary that's over 100 years old. This estate is famous for their virgin white tea but produces 40 different types of tea, with our ticket tea and piece of cake was included. The chocolate cake and tea was delicious a 10/10. I more have an appreciation of tea and the ancient techniques the estate uses to make and produce quality tea.
title: 10/10 for the tour, tea and cake

body: We were pleasantly surprised by the visit to this place, but I think it would not have been the same if it had been with another guide, the man who made the route was fantastic, I don’t remember the name unfortunately , he is 80 years old (he really seems 60) has been in the sector for 30 years and you rating that it fascinates him and that is by vocation completely. Ask for him when you go!
title: EXCEPTIONAL

body: Great trip and very interesting, the guide was so friendly and informative his name is ‏DagliEvery thing was wonderful and highly recommended
title: ‏Handunugoda, Ahangama

body: Very informative tour of working tea estate including plenty of history.Tea in old colonial bungalow welcome. Clear explanation of old and new equipment on display, and the stages from hand-harvest to sale.Array of many teas to taste afterwards - surprised they were all so different! We thoroughly enjoyed and recommend Handunugoda. Two hours was ideal for our visit.
title: Very enjoyable and informative tour of working lowland tea estate in southern Sri Lanka.

body: The reception was poor, the tour not very informative, the guide much too quickly (did not wait for all participants) answered our questions almost reluctantly. There was a tea to taste after a short walk to return to the starting point afterwards. There we could watch a video as they offered the virgin white tea (was mentioned again and again and again for sale (50 gr. = about 50 EUR. !!). then tea tasting again and done. Cost EUR 2.00 per person (not much but there was also not much to see, hear and read).The only thing we liked was the way from the coast to the Estate and back.
title: Boring not interesting tour

body: Nice visit with an employee passionate about what he does, small group tour, we saw the old-fashioned machine factory and enjoyed teas. It's local and we love it! I recommend +++
title: Great!

body: Went here as a surprise treat for my parents who had done a tea plantation trip 30 years ago thinking that it would only be them that enjoyed themselves. Had a lovely guided walk through the plantation, a cup of tea at the top, walk back down and a tour of the factory. Would highly recommend a trip here
title: Tea plantation worth a visit

body: Lovely drive up to the plantation from the coast through country lanes and villages. The tour of the plantation was informative - saw cinnamon, jackfruit, rubber and coffee as well as tea! Just the right length (around an hour) which included a walk through the plantation, tea and cake on the owner’s terrace, a tour of the factory and tasting in the shop. Definitely worth a visit if you’re in the area.
title: Interesting visit - worth a detour!

body: Nice and informative tour of the plantation. Unfortunately, the man who took the lead was always very quick and did not wait for the group to get back together and then tell on. With toddler we had the feeling more often to hang behind and only noticed "half". Otherwise nice.
title: Beautiful tour

body: We spent a most enjoyable morning here being shown the wonders of the art of tea growing and a clear explanation by our excellent guide of the different types of tea being grown on the estate. It is world famous for it's White tea and this was explained in detailed.
title: A wonderful place to visit and see tea being grown.

body: We spent a great morning at the tea plantation! First, there was a short tour that included all the important information and explanations about the growth of tea plants. Then we had a piece of cake and a cup of home-grown tea before we could examine all the machines and the process of making tea. At the end you had the opportunity to taste about 30 types of tea! A great experience if you like tea!We were at the tea plantation about 9:00 am, which is highly recommended as we were then alone and enjoyed the tour, as well as being able to ask all sorts of questions. Around noon as we left, a lot of people came and there are about 30-40 people per tour.
title: Short, exciting tour and a perfect excursion if you love tea!

body: We had a lovely tour of the plantation with Dudley, including tea and cake at the bungalow. However, the tour is not free - it is now 650 Rupees per person.We enjoyed seeing all the ancient machines, which are still going after 145 years. Also it was interesting to take in the flora and fauna of the area including a pepper tree, a cacao tree and all kinds of hibiscus. It's certainly worth a day away from the beach to absorb some of Sri Lanka's history and culture.
title: Fascinating tea plantation

body: Amazing unique tea plant with some interesting history. Has more then 40 kinds of tea and the guided tour helped us in understand the nuances of each variety. Excellent experience
title: Tealeafed

body: A good tour of the estate and factory along with a cup of tea and cake. Prices of the tea seem a bit high but a worthwhile visit
title: Put this tour of an iconic tea estate on your list.

body: Thankyou Dudley for an interesting and informative tour. 30 plus years in the business and his passion was clear throughout. A wonderful place far from the madding crowd. We learnt a lot and tasted some wonderful tea. Well worth a visit.
title: Beautiful, interesting and informative

body: Handunugoda tea estate is a beautiful and serene destination for tea lovers. The lush greenery and well-maintained tea plants create a peaceful environment, perfect for a relaxing visit. The staff is friendly and knowledgeable “specially our tour guide Dudly”, who offers insights into the tea-growing and harvesting process.
title: Unforgatable day

body: We were able to visit this small family tea factory and very friendly A small tea tasting in the middle and then at the end The ticket is not expensive 2$ per person + donation only if you want
title: Visit + tasting

body: A nice tour of the property but be aware the drivers who recommend this are all getting a kick back on your purchases and there is pressure to buy for this reason. Besides a nice informative tour the tea itself that is sold is expensive and I think the tourists are being sold the "seconds" or floor sweepings as our purchases were very dusty tasting and we have thrown them away. Save your money for the high country tea plantations where the tour is still good but the tea is actually fantastic.
title: Nice Tour, Bad Tea

body: i really enjoyed my trip in the plantation. i was able to experience plucking of tea leaves and there are many options of tea to try. it so convenient for me because i only have little time to explore sri lanka and if you are in galle, its the perfect place nearby just to have a quick trip to tea plantation.
title: happy visitor

body: The trip was amazing the people were smiley and we got to see much of the company and taste the tea, which is certainly a unique experience and the guide was sweet as well as the other people there.
title: tea view

body: interesting to see how tea, vanilla, pepper and cinnamon are grown and in the case of rea processed. Charming knowledgeable staff who want you to enjoy yourself and learn. Also a very good comparative tasting at the end of the tour. Be sure to research the book ' the Suicide Club' describing the. current owner's ancestors betting away most of the estate on the turn of a card. If you are lucky, you will y current owner who is fascinating and a legend in the tea industry. The white tea is mightily expensive but worth it.
title: Fascinating to understand the white tea story

body: This tea garden is a lovely place to visit if you’re staying in the southern part of Sri Lanka. It was rich in nature and very beautiful. The tour guide was informative and it was organised well. You definitely get a lot for your money! Children went free. Only an hour long tour so perfect for a quick stop on the way if you’re heading that way.
title: A cute and picturesque place!

body: Excellent value for money. Very knowledgeable guide taught us a lot about the tea making process, while the tasting options at the end were very generous.
title: Interesting place!

body: We were staying at The Fortress Hotel at Koggala and decided to visit the Handunugoda Tea Plantation, as it was only 15 minutes by Tuk Tuk from the hotel. The visit started with a tour of the estate and an explanation of the various teas and spices grown there. The estate is best known for the production of the Virgin White Tea, which you get to taste at the end of the tour. The tour itself lasts about 30 minutes before a break for a cup of Oolong tea and a piece of chocolate cake. During this we had a visit from a vary tame Mongoose, which we think has a taste for cake!. We then were shown around the production facilities, which is mainly based on 150 year old equipment, which is still in use. Finally, you are taken to the tea tasting, where there were dozens of different teas to taste. The Virgin White Tea is very light to drink but very heavy on the wallet!. Overall the tea plantation is well worth a visit.
title: Tea Plantation visit

body: Excellent and informative tour - given by a super helpful guide. A short (easy) ramble through the plantation, passing cinnamon, vanilla, pepper and, of course, tea. 42 varieties of it. Oh, and a monkey. A break for a cuppa and cake, followed by a tour of the factory and the finale of tea tasting, and a little shop selling about 20 varieties of tea.Well worth the drive through the long and windy country lanes to get to.
title: Well worth the trip

body: So glad I took this tour. Tea, cake, short plantation walk and a visit to processing unit, which was interesting. We also sampled many teas in the shop.
title: Tea and cake on the tour!

body: Had a really good guide, who was happy to take questions and didn't rush us through.Tour was really interesting with a huge amount of information.Scenery up here was amazing and it is so very very peaceful.There was a lovely cup of sapphire oolong tea and cake, and both were really tasty.Little mongoose paid a visit and we also saw a different type sitting close by.The equipment was old and still working too. To see how it all came together from picking to machines to packing was great.The tasting part....in the shop they had every tea they do laid out to taste. Too many and the flavours became mixed as no way to really cleanse mouth between tea.That said there were some stunning teas to be tried.No hard sell in the shop either and for local produced, single estate tea pricing was very reasonable we thought.The cost of the guide, the tour and tea and cake.....an unbelievable £1.60 / 640LKR Stunning value and highly recommended
title: Interesting and amazing value

body: We recently visited the Herman Tea Plantation, Estate and Factory in Handunugoda, and it was a captivating experience. The tour included an in-depth look at the production of both black and green but also white tea. We were especially fascinated by our visit to the black tea factory, where we saw the journey of tea from freshly harvested leaves to finely sorted products.The plantation's diverse range of teas, enhanced with unique flavors like pepper, hibiscus, and cinnamon from the plantation, was impressive. The tasting session was a highlight, allowing us to savor different teas, including the exquisite Virgin White tea, which stood out as a special treat.We also appreciated the opportunity to see the tea plant nursery, adding to our understanding of tea cultivation from its very beginning. The beauty of the plantation, combined with the informative tour and warm hospitality, made our visit truly memorable. For anyone interested in the art and science of tea-making, Herman Tea Plantation Handunugoda is a must-visit destination.
title: Enriching Journey Through Tea

body: The plantation itself is nicely located near Ahangama. However, Bush does not look as impressive as in the mountains. Lovely buildings and tea testing have a remarkable volume of tea
title: Nice place and worth visiting if you do not have a chance to travel to the mountains and see high-growing tea plantation

body: This place is amazing. It is a beautiful plantation and we had an incredibly knowledgeable tour guide who gave such in-depth information into their tea growing (and flavouring - cinnamon, pepper, vanilla etc) as well as their tea making process. This was the highlight tour of trip into the south of Sri Lanka and highly recommend it to anyone, even if you don’t drink a lot of tea!
title: Highlight experience in South of Sri Lanka

body: Great visitTook an hour (journey from Galle was 45mis though great country side)Lovely people. Short walk, tea and cake, factory tour, tasting and shopNo hard sell. Cost is $2 per personLovely genuine guide, very helpful. You see every aspect from picking to packagimg
title: Fabulous

body: Beautiful experience. Absolutely loved it. Not overly touristy, a genuine tea plantation where tea is grown, dried, roasted and cut - loved the tour of the ‘factory’ absolutely fascinating. And of course the tasting was great.
title: Don’t miss it

body: Loved spending the morning visiting this tea plantation and learning about tea making process. Our guide Seena was so nice and helpful and we got to taste their special oolong tea with some delicious chocolate cake. Seeing all the old machines and how they are used was very cool and would not have imagined they are still standing after 150 years! Nice bonus is that the place is solar powered !!!!! Highly recommend :)
title: Interesting, informative and lovely people

body: Very nice place, the staff is very friendly!You enjoy a very good tea made on site with a piece of homemade chocolate cake... a real treat! All for €2.Tea store, authentic, to do!
title: White tea house

body: Fascinating tour with a break to have tea and cake followed by tasting. Really recommend this. All teas available to purchase
title: beautiful tea plantation with interesting tour

body: I read online about this Tea plantation and reasonable price for walking tour entry with cake and tea tasting followed by factory tour and shop.We visited with our tuck tuck driver who was not permitted to join the tour (not entirely sure of the true reason)!The guy conducting the walking tour was informative and the tea and cake was delicious!The factory was larger than thought with old machinery still in use and shown each stage of the process.The tasting and shop was nice to enjoy but prices of tea seemed very so high especially in dollars which was a shame as they would be perfect gifts if they were more reasonable!!
title: Informative

body: Amazing experience. Well worth the detour on the way to Galle. Our guide was delightful and so knowledgeable. Don’t miss
title: Fabulous morning in the beautiful plantation

body: Thank you soooo much . Everything was perfect, the staff is very nice. Interesting excursions. Beautiful nature .
title: Everything was perfect

body: Such a fun stop to learn more about a low grown tea plantation - we really enjoyed the tour by our knowledgeable guide Vellamuthu, who introduced us to the variety of vegetation being grown on the plantation, let us taste a whole gamut of teas and shared lots of interesting insights about the tea making process! The tour even included a slice of cake and a cup of their Sapphire Oolong tea - delightful! Highly recommend this stop if you're looking to learn more about tea and also about a really interesting process of cultivating white tea that referenced ancient Chinese methods.
title: Toteally awesome!

body: Great cake and tea. Cool Guide!Nice walk though the plantation with monkeys and cute dogs. Very fun!
title: Cool afternoon.

body: A very interesting tour provided by Romash, recommended for anyone visiting near the area. A range of teas toChoose from at the end.
title: Tea,tea,tea!

body: This is a must see - the tour guide has enormous knowledge about tea and makes the whole experience pleasant and seamless. The tea tastes amazing and the selection.
title: Come see this even if you don’t drink tea

body: Thr guide was very friendly and welcoming, the views are amazing and the tea also! Loved it!!! Would definitely recommend. :))))
title: The tea factory

body: Nice to see, we went by tuk tuk from the hotel, the man from the estate tells his story perfunctorily and very compulsively, along the way he picks pepper and does a quiz with what he picksHe shows all the machines and the tea process, including a cup of tea and cakeIt's fun, but the tuk tuk ride there was just as much fun
title: Time left

body: We started the tour with a cup of Sapphire Oolong tea and slice of chocolate cake. We then walked around the grounds with a very knowledgeable guide. As well as the tea plants, he pointed out all the different plants that are used to flavour some of the teas, such as cinnamon, lemongrass, jasmine, peppercorns and hibiscus.We saw the process of the tea production, using very old machinery, then had the pleasure of tasting a huge amount of very different flavoured teas. There is a charge of 2$ for the visit and we felt this was very good value.A very enjoyable and informative trip. Highly recommend.
title: Very informative, great to see the whole tea production process

body: Fantastic Tea estate with a very dedicated and scilled guide. Abillity to taste several different tea’s before you decide what to by.
title: Perfect visit from Galle,Unawatuna or Koggala

body: One of the best places to be visited, If you are interest on tea you can sea the process of tea making at this place. Also you can buy fresh tea in to a very reasonable prices
title: You can buy very good quality tea

body: We received a very informative tour of the grounds and factory, which still has some of the original machines! At the start we were given some delicious tea and cake, and then had the opportunity to try all the teas available at the end. Would highly recommend as a day trip from Galle or nearby.
title: Great, informative visit.

body: We had a lovely experience at the tea estate! Our guided tour was quick but informative and included a slice of cake & tons of tea. They also grow peppercorns and cinnamon, both of which you can get in their shop. The estate is beautifully lush and makes for a nice afternoon activity.
title: A beautiful, unique experience!

body: I am a Lankan. I went to this place today. With a foreigner. One person has to pay 2$ to see this. The price of tea here is very high. The driver and guides who come with foreigners also have to pay 2$ to see this. The guides here even take a photo as the tourists like. Not given the chance.
title: A place where only money is expected

body: Handunugoda Tea Estate is a great afternoon activity for anyone who slightly likes tea (by the end of the tour, you'll LOVE tea). The grounds are beautiful, with a variety of different tea plants for demonstrations. Inside the processing facility, you can watch as the teas are dried, sorted and prepared for distribution using both modern machines (able to measure the size of the leaves) and antique mechanics. It's all exceptionally interesting and positive as this is the source of livelihood for a great number of locals. In the shop, one can smell and taste various types of teas and actually purchase some of the Herman teas to take home...which I did and they're amazing. Can't wait to order more!!
title: Excellent tour about tea growing...and excellent teas for purchase

body: We had a lovely stroll in the tea plantation with a very knowledgeable guide. At the end of the walk you are treated for a cup of tea and a slice of cake at the owners house. From here you continue to the tea factory where the whole process is explained. It’s amazing! They work with 145 years old machines!!! At the end of the tour you can taste at least 20 different kind of teas and buy your souvenirs.The tour used to be free, but due to the difficult economical situation they have introduced a nominal entrance fee of 2 USD.
title: Pleasant outdoor activity

body: We’ve assays wanted to visit a tea plantation and this estate was perfect en route to Galle. The guide was knowledgeable and a proper character. We loved learning about the tea process and the cuppa on the veranda ( with chocolate cake ) The old factory was fascinating as were the old pieces of machinery still in use. We tasted and purchased tea in the shop at the end , mainly to support the estate but also as a memento of a great couple of hours.
title: I’m British- what’s not to love about tea

body: A great trip, information guide was greatFree tea and cake was an added extraI especially liked the fact you could taste all the different varieties of tea grownA nice shop at the end to by the unique tea's
title: Large variety of teas to taste

body: We absolutely loved our visit to this very special plantation. Had a great tour which was just the right length for our hot kids who at 8 and 11 didn’t exactly have a tea plantation on their list of to-dos!Plantation is extremely beautiful and on our little walk we saw lots of tea plants and also wildlife and herbs. Factory was really interesting too. The tea and amazing cake on the verandah was really welcome (kids loved it!) and the tea tasting was incredibly well done too with all the different teas available for tasting - again something the kids really enjoyed.Others have said the teas are expensive. All I can say is that in the UK they would cost a lot more so we certainly bought quite a few.A really fun visit for the whole family and easy to fit into the day if you’re in the Galle area.
title: Blown away

body: Never ever did we have any idea about tea and just what was required! This was an absolutely hidden gem and was just amazing. Thoroughly recommend this as a visit. Actually got to see tea being sorted and then tasted the product you just can’t ask for more!!!
title: An absolutely hidden gem! Well worth the visit!

body: Wow! A hidden gem! What a lovely afternoon and how much we learned. Looking at the plants, learning about the types of tea, seeing the processing plant, a cup of tea and chocolate cake as well as tea tasting at the end. Please buy tea when you’re there as the tour is free and this is least we can do to repay a free, informative tour. Thank you to all.
title: Interesting, informative and engaging

body: Driving through small local villages and communities describe closely how's life on Sri Lanka. Plantation is beautiful and peaceful place you should visit and learn more about tea. Delicious tasing (cake and tea), guided tour through the plantation were very educative and interesting. You'll se the factory inside and on the end - you may taste tea samples to choose which one is the best for you. It's not about the one - you should buy more. All are delicious planted with love.
title: Awesome Virgin White tea plantation

body: We spent a lovely morning here guided around by the Manager David. He gave us a so much information and clearly loves the place, more than just a job. We saw lots of spices and wild life during our walk. Fascinating story of the history of Tea and the White Silver Tips.A beautiful cup of tea with excellent cake was enjoyed @ the owners residence, followed by a tour of the factory which was also extremely interesting. This followed a venture into the Tea Shop where the many teas manufactured were available for tasting and purchase. Which naturally did.
title: Very Informative

body: The place is beautiful and the tour they offer for free is extremely interesting: it covers info from planting to processing, showing breathtaking antique machinery that is still in use nowadays. They even offer a tasting with a slice of cake in the patio of a beatiful cottage, everything is organised with love and care. The shop is full of temptations (gorgeous products) and if you are lucky, as we were, you will meet the founder of this perfect place. A must go if you are in Galle or Unawatuna, we went by motorbike and it was really worth it!
title: Really interesting experience

body: This was an amazing visit of this family tea estate - we came without previous notice (in the Covid era - we were there completely alone) and the manager showed us around, explained the tea planting and tea making process...he spoke a good English. The tour, which was free of charge (tip if you liked it), was finished by tea tasting - we could taste every single tea they sell and then buy what we liked. :))
title: Amazing family tea estate!

body: Fantastic little trip. Enjoy having a walk around the plantation and seeing how the process of the tea making takes place. Free guided tour and then buy some tea at the shop. Worth the trip.
title: Tea trip

body: Another tea estate we thought but we were really glad we decided to come here. You are taken by tuk tuk and given an individual tour of the plantation and given a great cup of tea along the way. You then go tothe factory where you can see, touch and smell the tea making process which was fascinating. You also learn about the Virgin White Tea which this estate is famous for. There was a shop at the end but there was nopressure to buy anything. There were numerous teas available for taste testing, which we did, and ended up buying some , including the Virgin White Tea. We also bought a great souvenir inthe form of a book called The Suicide Club which is the story of the founder, and thattoo was very enjoyable.
title: A great place to visit

body: Although this is a free place to visit, it is not useful to visit there. 1) Actually this is situated in Down South, therefore the climate is not good for a quality product. - the best Ceylon tea we can found in Hill country.2) If you visit here you can get an actual experience of a real tea factory. This place will mislead you and will give wrong information.3) When comparing the price with the best tea in Sri Lanka, this is very expensive.4) Also the staff is not friendly.5) Finally I'm saying this is kind of a scam that will mislead you.
title: Wasting of time to visit here...

body: This was a unique experience! The gentleman who welcomed us asked where are we from and then greeted us and told us to follow him in our own language! Such a nice man, he was making an effort to learn words in all kind of languages. The estate is so beautiful, besides the tea we saw rubber tree, pepper plant. They served us with tea and cookies, showed old equipment, it was relaxing and educational.
title: We speak your language!

body: We arrived early (no booking) in the morning and was welcomed and informed of the specialty of the plantage the White Virgin. Then another guide took us around the plantage telling us about the different teas, how they grow and are picked. Me and my husband were the only guests.On the terrace to a beautiful house we were served oolong tea and cake for free.We were introduced to the manufacturing in the factory and then the tea tasting of 40 different types! Very interesting! You don’t have to buy the tea from the shop they have shipping through their website.Before you leave you donate a voluntary sum, no individual tip is allowed. It was a great experience- lot to see and learn, so nice breathing fresh air and walking in the lush plantation. Recommended!
title: Very nice visit

body: We are so impressed that this plantation is offering tours for free. The guide was so knowledgeable and they even gave us tea and cake. It was a pleasant way to spend an hour or two and we learned a lot as well
title: Really interesting

body: Nice experience but it will not be the same with the best guide ever! Istouti so much Sellamuthu !!!
title: Nice experience!

body: Really interesting to learn a little about the history and techniques used within the tea plantation. Even 40 different teas to try - the Masala Chai flavoured tea was my favourite!
title: Intersting

body: Well I cant believe all the good reviews of this place, I will tell you how it was for us. We arrived around 8.20 am no one was around. Our driver went off to find someone we were then told quite curtly by an older gentleman guide that we were too early and would have to wait ( your website clearly says tours start at 8am) We were asked to sit in the shop on damp cushions and given a tatty dog eared sheet explaining all the teas they manufacture. About 15 mins later we summoned by the guide just the two of us as no one else had arrived who fleetingly told us about the virgin tea, peppercorns and cinnamon. He told us that 100 people worked on the estate. He then walked us up to the bungalow at record speed passing just 2 x pickers. I had to be quick to take photos as he was desperate to keep going. Tea and cake was served at the bungalow...might be a heathen but tea was awful prefer my Yorkshire blend. We were taken to the so called factory, not one machine was in operation or staff working when do they manufacture all this tea? my doubts are not here looking at the ancient machinery. We also entered there with no hair nets strategically placed were pots of tea leaves of which he put some into my sweaty hand for me to pour it back...yuck !!!We were then had to trudge back down to the shop to sample all the teas. Cant say I was enthralled with any of them bar one. We decided to buy one box you could tell the guide was upset that's all we were spending so tried to get us to buy cinnamon sticks, we have our own catering business back home and have buckets of cinnamon. Disappointed with what we were going to buy he walked off..no goodbyes etc etc Came away with little knowledge the place is run down, glad we only stopped here enroute to National park would have been miffed if we had paid a taxi or tour guide to take us here. Whilst this is free run by volunteers this place is just a ploy to sell tea.
title: Don't waste your time

body: Taken by tuk tuk. Enjoyed the tour. Interesting way they use a symbiotic relationship between the various tea plants and other vegetation
title: Interesting tour

body: Really nice tour (free) where we visited tea plantations, factory tasting areas and of course the shop. Really enjoyed it.
title: Great tour

body: A beautiful frozen in time Tea Estate, we arrived and where greeted by a guide that walked us along the White Tea plantation and showed us the Rubber trees and Cinnamon trees.We saw women harvesting the tea leaves by hand and heard various explanations.Then we arrived at a beautiful colonial style villa at the top of the hill where we got a peace of cake and cup of delicious tea, after relaxing in the cool breeze we toured the villa saw a Mongoose crossing the path and went down to the tea factory witnessing the same 150 year old machines still working today drying and separating the tea leaves.And finally ended up at the shop where we tasted all of the tea varieties and bought some tea to take with us.
title: A working Tea Estate Museum

body: We came here early in the morning and there was only a couple of people in our group, the guide was friendly and informative, the tea tasting and cake was in a lush garden setting, the factories that still use the original machinery in excess of 100 years old makes the product so much more authentic in my opinion
title: Add it to your list, go early morning

body: Nice place. The staff is well trained. There are neat signboards telling you how to tip. The place is well maintained. It was great for the kids as they got to taste several teas and understand the process.
title: Great visit

body: Virgin Tea Plantation - interesting story,good guidance, original machinery, super degustation for free
title: Specila tea plantation

body: We went here with our young children on the recommendation of some locals, more in hope than expectation.Anyway we arrived and had a guided tour of how the tea leafs are grown, tried a few local teas in a nice sat down area.Followed by a tour of the factory where the leafs are dried out and made into the tea we drink.There is no charge for this service, and it’s made quite clear not to tip any individual, if you want to tip there is a box at the end.There is a store at the end, which sells various tea related items, there is absolutely no hard sell what so ever, really enjoyable due to this.We brought some tea to take, would definitely recommend this as a way to spend a few hours.
title: Great place to go

body: Perfect for a guided tour with a quick look on how tea is manufactured and great souvenir shop to buy some tea for the family
title: Best Tea Plantation in the area

body: We had been to the tea plantation on a number of occasions. Right off the bat - it is a great and insightful tour, that is also complimentary and will take about 60-120 minutes. The tea selection that is produced on-site is grand and the facilities are nice to explore.Generally there are no set times (it’s upon arrival and tour guide availability). The first time we went was during off-season (as a couple) - this meant that there were fewer tourists. This was also reflected in the tour (with the same guide mind you). He was more thorough (more informative) and took his time - then it lasted close to 2 hours. The second time we went was in December (beginning of the season) and it was completely different. We went as a group (of 8 incl a 3 and 4 year old). We arrived simultaneously with a larger tourist group. This time the tour was rushed (a bit more challenging when you have 2 little one’s). When we made it up to the house for the tea tasting and cake, part of the porch was covered off and there was some noisy construction work going on - wonder why they couldn’t have done it during off-season? The porch got crowded as the other tour group caught up and we had to hurry through the facilities and back as there was another group coming.I did see that they had a kids camp under construction - I think that is a great idea and will make this a more well-rounded family experience, something we lacked on our 2nd visit. Nonetheless, good experience and would recommend it (if they more guides during peak times).
title: Great tea tour (though not during season)

body: Very interesting experience and lovely teas for tasting.The stuff was very friendly and we hat a great stay there.
title: Very interesting experience

body: Fascinating tea plantation with free tours by employees. It was great to walk around the estate and find out how they planted, harvested and maintained the tea and associated crops. It was quite a place to visit.
title: Ver Interesting plantation

body: We had an excellent visitTea explainationsSpycies also (pepper, coffee, cinnamon...)Living Museum with how to dry, crush and sieveIt was very interesting and adapted for children
title: Perfect visit

body: This is something I love to do with all friends and family who come and visit us. It's a working tea factory and it's really cool to see how it all works.
title: Free tour!

body: We had a great time touring this wonderful plantation despite the overcast weather. Our guide, Meril, was patient with our many questions and very informative in his responses. We stopped and watched the rain past whilst having a cup of nice hot - you guessed it - oolong tea and chocolate cake. We loved the many varieties of tea. Be warned: the shop wasn't cheap (!) but there was no pressure to buy. Overall, we recommend it.
title: Insightful

body: We had an amazing experience at the Herman Tea Factory. We were lucky enough to be shown around the plantation by Meril, a knowledgeable gentleman who spoke wonderful English. He knew all about the process and the local flora and had a great sense of humour. It was a private quiet tour and we went at our own pace and asked as many wuestoins as we wanted. The tea tasting as very interesting and the shop had a wide variety of teas for purchase. The tour was truly made wonderful by Meril however. Beautiful location, highly recommended.
title: Amazing Experience

body: We went to a tea plantation in Sri Lanka,never realising what an amazing experience this would be.We got there just as they were closing,and a most characteristic man told us,he would take us round.The tale of the white tea was fascinating,the guide was so informative,and eventually,it transpired,he owned the plantation,though was modest enough not to tell us.We had tea and cake at his house,he showed us the BBC clip of the background if his exclusive tea,it was a most special experience.I can't tell you if it will be Herman that gives you the tour,but if it is,you have won the golden ticket!!Most interesting, well worth seeing.
title: Coffee drinker converted

body: This was a detour visit during our SL vacation. As we dropped out the Whale Watching, we googled this place and asked our cab buddy to take us there. The plantation is well kept, just like others, as it is a major source of revenue generation in SL.The plantation tour takes about 45 mins. includes a free tea and cake serving also. After this, they take you through the tea factory, which for me was done in a quite haphazard manner. Later, as expected, they take you to their main shop where there are about 50 samples kept for tasting. 50! Seriously???? After the entire tour and smells around, I bet your taste bud would not be able to differentiate between more than 3-5 samples.Anyways, if you are on a long tour in SL, visit the Blue Field Tea factory [between Nuwara and Kandy].... it is much better there. you also get to pluck the leaves and is very decently explained by the factory's person.
title: Good insight into Tea Plantation. Expensive Sri Lankan Tea though.

body: The tour of the plantation was fantastic. We saw the tea crops and the ladies hand picking the tips to make beautiful tea. We learnt about the production and was able to taste a variety of tea. They have a very expensive white tip tea that is only sold in an exclusive cafe in Paris. The tea was delicious. An enjoyable experience.
title: Lovely tour and tasting

body: This estate is 200 acres and they produce white tea, black tea, natural rubber & cinnamon. The machines they use is from UK, quite old but still functioning. Our tour guid was Meril, nice, knowledgable person with a smile on his face. Meril took us everywhere in that estate showing and explaining all the trees there and how the grow, pick and produce tea; how they collect rubber from trees; the process of cinnamon making and invited us for a nice cup of tea, which was his favorite. We finished our tour with drinking maybe 20 (if not more) cups of different teas and bought some to take back with us. Its a feee entrance place but they appreciate a donation which shouldn’t be to individuals but to put into the box in the shop which will be contributed equally to the staff. Peaceful green place with a lot of birds, peacocks, flowers and heavenly beautiful view. Loved every minute of spending there.
title: Amazing experience

body: Visited this tea plantation during our stay in Galle and it was fabulous. The tour guide walked us through all aspects of tea processing and took us through the plantation where there were lots of photo opportunities. Afternoon tea was served with a delicious choc cake and lastly we given a full tea tasting experience. There was no charge for the tour, but donations were encouraged.
title: A complete experience

body: We visited this tea plantation in March 2018. We were in Sri Lanka during a time of torrential rain, so our guided tour was aided by umbrellas! We were greeted with warmth and care, and set off to discover the plantation and all that it has to offer. We were shown how the tea was picked and made in the factory. After the tour, we were able to visit the shop. We were under no pressure to buy, but we were amazed at the number of teas available to taste, and purchase. It was a far better tea plantation and tour than several others we visited. I would recommend Handunugoda Tea Estate to anyone wanting to learn from people who have a passion for tea.
title: Excellent tour, friendly guide!

body: We went here by tuk tuk from Galle. The guide was informative, funny and showedus many thinks. we saw the tea pickers which were fascinating to watch. We then enjoyed a cup of tea and chocolate cake before looking in the small factory. We all enjoyed this trip even our 15 year old granddaughter.thank you all.
title: Fabulous tour

body: My friends and I get here from center of Ahangama around 20mins by tuktuk, the local guide is so nice and friendly, he can speak many languages which he made guest who visit here were more comfortable.Gave many important information on differents kinds of tea in plantation area, including pepper, rubber, hibicus,etc. And last part is about tea shop, good to taste many cups of tea. End up buy the combination of many taste which called "TEA Flirt"Recommend to visit to see local plantation and relaxing naturePrair B from Thailand
title: Tea factory ;friendly people and nice tase of teas

body: We made this a part of our day touring between Galle and Weligama and in the first instance we were surprised that tipping was discouraged, a donation was promoted at the conclusion of the tour but no pressure. The estate is a working property so you see people going about their business while learning how white & black tea is made. After walking through the plantation we were treated to a cup of oolong tea and a piece of chocolate cake, very appreciated. Afterwards we were given a tour of the factory with machines still operational after a hundred years. There was the mandatory visit to a tasting room and shop but I reiterate, we never felt under any pressure to buy or donate, although we did. An hour or so well spent.
title: Tea for Two

body: The stroll through the tea bushes is not as striking as in an altitude plantation, but you can see several spice trees and plants on the way. The factory machines are more than a century old and still in use. The tea shop is a treat for any quality tea lover.It's all free, and there's a tip jar by the cashier, split among the staff, if you are happy.
title: Factory with old colonial flair. Great tea tasting

body: Do you want to know where and how white, green, black tea is produced? Do you want to know the history of Sri Lankians tea? Do you want to taste different kinds of local tea? And all that for free. So this is the place you definitely must visit. You won't be disappointed. Tasty tea, interesting insights into tea production with great guide is what you'll get. I enjoyed it a lot.
title: Amazing experience

body: Amazing experience. It’s a beautiful tea plantation, very interesting history, facts about tea and the other spices and rubber they grow. The tour was great fun, including sampling the many teas they produce. They took us through the entire process of growing and making tea. We saw how cinnamon sticks are made. Highly recommended.
title: Tea Plantation

body: This tea farm/factory is a bit out of the way to get to but none the less exciting. Very interesting to see tea in its raw form before its dried, heated and eventually packaged for consumers. Highly recommend going to see the tea making process. The staff is awesome and very knowledgeable. At the end of the roughly 15 minute tour there is a tea tasting room and gift shop. Lots of items and teas to choose from. Great experience!!!
title: Amazing experience!

body: We visited the Tea Estate at the end of a one day tour of Galle and its surroundings. It was just a flying visit but we saw the plants, the drying houses and machinery used in making the tea. At the end of the tour we had the chance to taste the teas and buy the product. Sri Lanka is famous for its tea and so a visit to a plantation is essential. It was interesting and I do not think we would have got anymore from the the visit if we had been there longer.
title: Just a taster!

body: I never knew how we got tea!! What an experience! I was disappointed that we didn't get to taste the different teas. I would have given 5 stars for the opportunity to tase a variety. Perhaps for a fee you could taste 5 different teas. Like a flight of beer! We bought several teas and were not disappointed at all.
title: I had no Idea

body: A really enjoyable day! Much more informative than a similar tea station we visited in India. Our guide Xavier was fabulous, he was fluent in many languages and took time to explain everything to us about 'tea' growing and processing. He answered happily all my questions and we were not rushed. We were so pleased to meet and watch a group of lovely ladies 'plucking' the tea and placing it in their bags hung from their heads and hanging down their backs. Xavier also guided us and explained about the rubber (latex) plantation, with many jokes too regarding it's uses! We learnt about growing and harvesting pepper, cinnamon and pineapples - all so very interesting information. We then went to the factory and were proud to see their 145 year old machines, made in Sheffield, UK still running smoothly. We watched ladies doing a lot of hand processing within the factory and seeing warm, black tea being produced and watching it's different stages to completion. We were then invited to enjoy a proper china cup of their Oolong Ruby tea and a slice of lovely chocolate cake - mmm! We then 'tasted' around 50 freshly brewed teas made at Hermans - amazing! The shop is beautifully presented and no pressure at all to buy - though I am very happy with the tea I bought. Tip - they only take cash and no cards.Thank you to everyone involved in our totally 'free' guide around your interesting tea station.Thank you Caroline
title: Excellent!

body: We came here as recommended in the lonely planet guide and by friends! We had Xavier as our guide and he was incredibly knowledgeable about all of the trees and teas and we were astonished by his ability to fluently speak so many different languages! We were given a choice about whether we wanted to go on a short or long tour - our group chose the long tour and it was interesting to learn about all of the products that this plantation grows. Tea and cake at the bungalow was a nice touch but the real highlight was the factory! We were able to see the old machines working and the different processes were explained in detail to us. We were then taken to the shop where we were able to taste all of the teas that we could buy, I didn't feel pressured to buy anything, however I am extremely happy with what I did buy! The bags that are given to you are lovely souvenirs and you are also given several information sheets about the plantation and their teas! Definitely recommend a visit!
title: Interesting tour and very knowledgeable guide!!

body: While in the former Ceylon, must get to a Tea Plantation. The very basic tour is free and so is the tea tasting, which was fantastic. The plantation is approximately 20km from Galle and easy to get there by tuk tuk.
title: Worth a visit - complimentary tour and tea tasting.

body: We visited today, the tour was very rushed, the guide knew his stuff but it was very basic. The tour of the factory was interesting with some very old machinery still in everyday use. The shop and tea tasting was very informative. Overall worth a visit but don’t expect too much.
title: Free tour

body: We called here after a recommendation by a tuk tuk driver. It was a very pleasant and informative visit. Our guide took great pride in his knowledge and use of many languages. We stopped half way round for a cup of oolong tea which we both enjoyed. Next, a visit to the factory where we were shown many various machines for the production of the tea from drying leaves to the finished product. The next part was tea tasting and there was many to choose from including vodka tea. Very interesting. Free to visit here and no pressure at all to buy anything.
title: Nice Visit - Great vodka Tea

body: An interesting tour of the plantation and little factory, with a cup of tea and cake thrown in, ending in a nice shop with opportunity to taste lots of teas and tea-related gifts.
title: Fun (free!) tour

body: A visit on route from Hambantota to Columbo and well worth it. Fascinating insights into tea and lots of other lovely delights - including pepper! Superb guide who knows everything about the tea and factory and a cup of tea and lovely piece of cake. A must see trip if you've in Sri Lanka.
title: An incredible few hours on route to Columbo

body: Enjoyed the tour of the tea plantation and came away knowing more about the topic and having sampled a range of interesting types. The tour is free and includes a guided trip round the property with well informed guide, tea and cake in the garden (they had me at "cake") and a tasting session of products available in the shop. Very nice low key and no hard selling.
title: Tea Party

body: We got almost no information of how the tea plants are grown and about the production process. We just rushed through the plantation. Seemed like they were only interested in selling their white tea. Not worth the travel!
title: Tea plantation

body: A nice excursion, conservative tea ceremony in the midday heat in the shade of trees, good shop with many sorts. You can try all of them before buying. Not expensive. Much cheaper than in the airport and the website.
title: Worth going

body: Very friendly staff on arrival. Free tour through the plantation with chocolate cake and tea in the garden halfway through the tour. The factory section is impressive as they turn the machines on to demonstrate if they aren’t running. The end of the tour involves a tasting of over 30 different teas including the expensive white tea. Very well organized and informative. Define recommend.
title: Great Tea Experience

body: good place to visit. the manager was excellent and explained the whole process. we had a lovely time. Thank You.
title: wow!

body: This is a lovely experience. Free tour of plantation and traditional tea processing with informative guide (ours was Meril). Very interesting to see tea but I also really enjoyed seeing peppercorns, cinnamon, rubber, jackfruit, cashew nut and starfruit trees plus lots of birds, butterflies and lizards!Lovely cup of tea and chocolate cake. They ask for a donation to be shared amongst staff which we were more than happy to provide along with buying some tea. Thoroughly recommend.
title: Very enjoyable

body: We have been to many tea plantations in Sri Lanka and also Malaysia. This was one of the best! We not only learnt about tea, but also cinnamon, pepper and rubber! After a lovely walk, we sat down and enjoyed a cup of tea and a piece of cake (we had not paid for anything thing yet!). The tea tasting was fantastic- could sample all the teas for sale, and there was an information sheet to help you too. It was a welcomed change for this area to find somewhere so lovely, few people and no pressure to buy. Highly recommended.
title: Best tea estate!

body: Visited in 2013 and enjoyed it so much we visited again. Unfortunately, the tour is shorter than in the past and tea is no longer provided at the Gunaratne bungalow (Herman Gunaratne has written books about Sri Lanka that are well worth reading). However, the tea and cake (free) and the brief but informative tour still worth doing. It’s a very different experience from the tea plantations in the higher tea country so a must do activity to compare with Ella and Nuwara Eliya experiences. They are the only manufacturer of Virgin White tea which can be tasted along with many other varieties in their shop. They also sell Herman Gunaratne’s books along with other thoughtful souvenirs. The tour of the manufacturing process was excellent.
title: Enjoyable

body: If you are a tea drinker, then this is the place to go, with over 50 different types of tea, a truly wonderful interesting place, with great chocolate cake!
title: Interesting and stunning location, tea heaven!

body: Just back from Sri Lanka and visited Handunugoda Tea Plantation, so interesting to see the process from start to finish and taste some of the many offerings. Of particular note here is the Virgin White Tea - untouched by human hands from the harvesting through production to the caddy, produced at this estate and highly sought around the world. Our tour of the planation finished with a welcomed cup of Ruby Oolong tea and a chunky slice of delicious chocolate cake .... yum!Highly Recommended.
title: Tea Tasting Supreme....

body: Really wanted to get to a tea plantation while I was here in Sri Lanka. Handunugoda was raved about in town. It's about 40 minutes from Galle Fort. Free tour, hot tea and cake. You can sample up to 60 varieties and there are plenty to purchase.
title: A must do if you're in Galle

body: Having initially been quoted anything from 20 to 30 American dollars, which they said included the entrance fee we opted to be taken there by our trusted tuk tuk driver Isuru.On our arrival, having been driven through beautiful countryside and rice paddy fields we arrived at the estate to be met by a charming elderly Sinalese gentleman whose first words were, “ I am going to take you on a tour of the estate, it is completely free of charge”. The speciality tea is white tea. He walked us through the estate giving a running commentary on tea production, rubber and cinnamon production before we went to the plantation house where we sat down on the veranda to be served Ruby Oolong tea with milk accompanied by one of the nicest pieces of cake we have ever eaten. We went round the working factory with machines over 145 years old. I will not reveal further as the tour guide explains everything. After this we went to the shop and tasted 20 or more teas and purchased those we liked.
title: An authentic tea factory that is unique.

body: We visited this unique tea estate on our recent visit to Sri Lanka and would recommend it highly. I did not realise ho little I knew about the tea making process! The guides are well informed and friendly, and give a full tour of the estate, including the tea plantations, the tea processing factory and also include a stop at a quaint tea room on the estate (the chocolate cake was delicious!) You get the chance to sample over 20 different teas, and also to purchase them. A very educational and informative half day trip.
title: Very interesting tour of a very old tea estate

body: I had no idea I would enjoy a tea tour so much! We had a group of seven - went on the early bird tour- and everyone thoroughly enjoyed it. Merle, our guide, spoiled us with his plethora of knowledge...he was so very kind! We also saw some great wild life- a peacock in a tree- wild monkeys... The variety of tea is amazing - you will definitely find one of your liking. A definite must if you have a leisurely day to spend in Sri Lanka.
title: Tea for Seven

body: I thought I knew tea, until I came here! A short walk through the gardens to see how tea is grown, and peppercorns, and cinnamon, and jackfruit, and hibiscus, to sit down for a cuppa and some cake. Then a tour of the fascinating factory and a chance to taste so many different teas. The guides are very entertaining. Of course you will want to buy some to take home. We did.
title: Tea and more tea

body: It was very informative & beautiful scenery. Personal guide to show you around with taste testing of all the varieties. Had a great time
title: Day trip

body: We were shown around the plantation by an informative guide, served tea and cake at the homestead which was relaxing, then shown through the tea factory and to the gift shop at the end where you could try all sorts of teas. The whole thing was free but they have a donation box at the end and tips are shared between all the guides, which was a nice way to do it. We thoroughly enjoyed it, even our daughter who does not like tea. Beautiful part of the world but a bit tricky to find.
title: A highlight of our trip

body: Really wanted to visit a tea plantation not too far from Bentota. Far exceeded my expectations. The people were so kind, patient, informative - and not obviously interested in your money, so unlike the culture I am used to. The guide showed us through the plantation, the tea, rubber, herbs, explaining key points. We were given ta and cake! The factory, comprising of British Empire imported machinery, still in use, was so interesting. The shop was a final stop with a huge selection of tea tasting set out for us. There was really no expectation of us to buy, but what we did buy was the best tea I have tasted. Wish I had bought more. The highlight of my holiday.
title: A jewel of Sri Lanka

body: I didn’t initially expect to enjoy this visit to the tea plantation and joined my family to check it out.We started off on a free tour around the tea plantations where we could see the locals picking the tea. The tour guide was informative, funny and spoke serval languages exceptionally well.We were shown the machinery and how the tea process making worked, which I found very interesting.We were then taken to the tea testing room, where I tried approx 35 different and unique teas, which were all exceptionally We were then given the option to buy them.Thoroughly recommend this trip. Great if your staying near Galle or Bentota.
title: Great trip

body: It is a free tour although you have the option to leave a small token in the tea tasting room. It is a very pleasant stroll to the tea house, where along the way they also show you collecting sap from rubber trees. The view from the tea house is pretty special and you are served cake and your choice of teas.The walk through the tea processing building is very interesting with some of the machinery being 148 years old and having manufactured by the same company that built the Titanic. You also get the opportunity to taste a range of teas at the end of the tour. Well worth a visit as the tuktuk ride up there takes you through the country side but is not very far from the toen.
title: Surprising and interesting

body: On a private Tuk-Tuk tour our driver took us to the Handunugoda Tea Estate. The tour guide was very informative and showed us around the estate showing us the various plants, and how they make tea. We were then served chocolate cake and tea which were both really nice. We then tasted around 40 different teas in the visitors centre. I’d recommend the masala tea. Overall a good experience.
title: Tea Tasting

body: We had a very knowledgeable guide who explained all about the different types of tea and we had a slice of chocolate cake and cup of Saphire Pekoe on the owners verandah before going to the factory and then tasting all 50 varieties of tea they produce. Of course there is a shop to buy if you want but no high pressure sales. Highly recommended.
title: Great tour

body: Loved the personal tour. The authentic tea estate and factory. Very well organised and friendly. Complimentary cup of tea and cake.
title: So many teas to taste

body: I was interested to read the comments in these pages from the Poor and Average contributors.They may have a point. It seemed to be a long way to go for little reward. On arrival a quick walk up the hill for a cup of tea and chocolate cake with a brief explanation of the Estate's purpose on the way. Down again to the factory (impressive machinery by the way). Taste something cold and wet and leave avoid paying LKR800 (£3.60 or thereabouts) for a few grams of tea leaves. I suppose first time visitors to a plantation may be impressed.If you really want to be impressed, travel to the Kandy/Newara Eliya regions in Central Province. Camellia Sinesis as far as the eye can see.
title: If you in the area.........

body: I’ve been to a number of tea estates as a child during visits to Sri Lanka and assumes they were all in the hill country in the centre of the island; so I was very surprised to find the Handunugoda Tea Estate near Galle. Upon arriving we were greeted by one of the team who showed us around the grounds where tea, coffee, cinnamon and even rubber are grown. The staff were accommodating and friendly, even giving our family a sample of tea and chocolate cake before we were shown around the factory and then into the purchasing area where you can sample just about all the teas that are grown here. Really interesting visit and great tea! Recommended
title: Very Nice Working Tea Estate

body: We were staying in Galle and took a taxi which took about 40 minutes. Xavier led our tour and was very knowledgeable about all aspects of the plantation. We had a few different nationalities in our group and Xavier was able to communicate with all of them. The tea and cake on the veranda was a lovely touch and a chance to chat to others in the group. The whole process of getting the tea from picking to packaging was fascinating and the 140 year old machinery still being used daily was a sight to behold. After a tour of about an hour we were led to the gift shop for a chance to taste many different teas and purchase if we wanted. This was so helpful and meant we didn't buy the ones we didn't like the taste of. Most of the teas were reasonably priced although some of the more specialised were a bit more expensive. And really, if you're getting a free tour why wouldn't you want to buy something as a thank you. As for the tip jar, well this is shared by all the employees on the plantation so why not give generously and help these lovely people to have a little extra for their families. I don't understand why some people complain about being pressured - there was absolutely no obligation to buy anything. We had very memorable couple of hours - thank you Handungoda.
title: Great experience

body: I disagree with all the comments saying the tour guide was pushy - our tour guide was lovely and gave us a very informative tour. We talked us through all the different plants and teas made, the *FREE* tea and cake was delicious and the plantation was beautiful. Yes they take you to the gift shop at the end but there was no pressure at all to buy anything. Would recommend highly to anyone who is in the area!
title: Wonderful tour, friendly guide

body: Not very informative. Pushy guide. We had a much more interesting tour in Ella. Nice tea and cake though. Expensive tea in the shop.
title: Only visit if no time for the Hill country

body: The tour of this tea plantation was recommended to us and we found it to be very informative. The guide was able to speak a large number of languages and initially showed us around the plantation, teaching us about the history, the cultivation of virgin tea, various other plants and trees in the area. During this tour we went to a plantation bungalow where we were given tea (to drink) and cake. The tour continued in the buildings, where the British equipment was still working and ended in watching a short video, sampling the numerous teas and checking out the teas on sale.We thought the teas were quite expensive, if they had been a more reasonable price I think more tourists would have purchased them for gifts. (This was the same in other tea plantation shops).
title: Well worth a visit

body: Very interesting tour around the Handunugoda Tea Estate. Not only learnt about their unique tea but also saw coffee plants, teak and rubber trees, pepper plants and cinnamon. Our guide was excellent, informative and friendly. Tea and delicious cake at the plantation house was lovely. A vast selection of teas were available to taste following the tour of the tea processing. So glad we went- couldn’t believe it was free! Don’t hesitate to go.
title: Interesting and fun

body: We stopped here on part of a tour and it was excellent. Our guide was great and explained all about the tea. It was a nice touch to get to try the tea and have some cake before looking at the actual factory and then the shop. You also get to try lots of teas. Definitely worth a visit!
title: Great place

body: Been to this place multiple times over the years and it is always a lovely experience. Herman, the owner, is a real character too. Well worth putting on your itinerary if you are in the Southern Province.
title: Visit with kids

body: We visited the tea estate for an afternoon with the family. Perfect way to spend an afternoon. Very helpful guide explained the process of tea production, from the tea pluckers to the drying room. Tea and delicious cake in the very pretty garden, with flowers and birds. Finally tea tasting and the opportunity to purchase. We even had an extra tour round the estate looking for peacocks! A really lovely afternoon.
title: Excellent Informative Afternoon

body: I use trip advisor all the time but rarely write posts. This however is worth writing. The tea factory & plantation are well worth a visit, it’s very uncrowded unlike some of the bigger places and the tour guides are exceptionally knowledgable. All the staff were extremely friendly and even though obviously a business and the tour is free, we didn’t pressure to buy anything! We bought & tipped because both the tea & tour were very good quality.
title: Well worth a visit

body: Well worth a visit. Our guide (Meril) was very knowledgable and there was no pressure to buy tea at the end of the tour (although of course we did!) Just to taste over 20 teas was a great experience but the chocolate cake at the owner's house was perfect!
title: Fascinating and free!

body: Great place to stop off for a couple of hours and to meet the staff and to learn about the production of tea. We were guided around the facility by Xavier - thoroughly knowledgable and a source of information throughout. The opportunity to sit and to eat cake and drink tea in such beautiful and stunning scenery after a long drive was extremely welcome. The location itself is completely isolated - surrounded by the most idyllic and enchanting scenery. The shop itself is not overpriced and you continue to have the opportunity whilst in there to try all different types of tea. No pressure to purchase.
title: A Gem Of The Trip

body: We visited the tea estate, which is down a narrow road through the lush green Sri Lankan countryside. The tour was free, and the tour guide was great with my children, making sure they were included. We were shown the tea plants themselves (as well as Hibiscus, Cinnamon, Coffee plants and others) and then seated for some tea and chocolate cake. My 16-year-old was a little nonplussed until the cake arrived...Afterwards we visited the factory which was great-the machinery is 140 years old and the process is more or less unchanged. There was a shop at the end where you could taste every variety of tea they make, but no pressure to buy.
title: A nice way to spend an hour or so

body: We thoroughly enjoyed the free tour with our guide Xavier. He was very knowledgeable about the whole process and particularly proud of their traditional methods, particularly the virgin white tea.The tea and chocolate cake were delicious and the tasting session was enjoyable too. There was no pressure to buy in the shop, but of course we did! I’m looking forward to trying my Suicide Club tea!
title: Tea Plantation Tour

body: Please, please visit! The tour is free and they take you on the most charming tour through the estate, you get to see cinnamon trees, rubber trees, cocoa trees, etc! They have beautiful gardens with flowers, and with tea of course! It's a lovely way to spend an afternoon!
title: FREE AND AMAZING

body: This is a small holding tea estate, but has Variety of other plants and spices. The Manager David has Depth knowledge of tea Industry and Productions, This Place easy to visit from Your Coastal hotel. The owner Herman Gunaratne a legendary tea planter, who started his planting days during the British Raj. A visit will make you to realise Sri Lanka is a different country.
title: The Ceylon Tea

body: This is a lovely way to see a tea plantation. Our guide was knowledgeable and friendly. He showed us the different types of leaves and described the different ways to make tea as well as how their specialty tea was created and it’s health benefits. There is a tea and cake stop halfway through which is nice. You are then able to try a large variety of teas with no pressure to buy. A nice morning out.
title: A fun outing

body: You hear a lot of good of this place, but you try reaching this place to visit is a big challenge, some times with traffic conditions so bad these days its hard to reach this destination in time, and the staff are not at all understanding, they work very strictly to their times, if you are five minutes late they tell you go and fly a kite type of attitude, I think it is one place to avoid as they have lost their charm that they used to have when they first started. i personally will avoid this place, as there are other tea estates to visit in close proximity who give you a better service and a better and warm welcome.
title: Visiting is a challenge

body: We enjoyed our tour of this unique tea plantation. Merle our guide was fantastic and so generous with his time. The chocolate cake and welcome tea was a nice touch. This plantation is in a truly beautiful location ... a little tricky to find. The teas are fantastic so we stocked up.
title: Great outing

body: Was given a tour of the Virgin White Tea Plantation by Meril, who was very friendly and knowledgeable. Did not realise they made so many varieties of tea on the estate, also the numerous other flowers and trees they had growing. Tour is free but a request is to leave a tip in the jar of the shop at the end; it gets divided between all staff. Loved how they have a dedicated carer for a lame ex-racehorse that lives on site, and enjoyed tea and cake with Lara the Golden Lab. Beautiful site and location. Found it really interesting that they use mostly the same technology for processing the tea as when they first started over a hundred years ago. A great finish is the tasting session at the end of the tour. Would recommend a visit by anyone wanting to see a working tea plantation.
title: Worth visiting

body: Our local guide stopped us as something interesting to do and he was so right. It's entrance free and the guide showed us everything, tea, rubber trees, flowers, coffee you name it! He offered is a free cup of a spectacular oolong tea and some cake before they took us to the factory where you very to see how the tea is made. Loved every second!
title: So interesting

body: There is something for everyone on this tour. Whether you are interested in the full process of plant to packet tea manufacture, tasting and comparing many different teas, hearing the history of tea in Sri Lanka or enjoying the wildlife that thrives here - you'll find it on this plantation. Our guide Meril was a wealth of knowledge and very friendly and you could see that he was very proud of what this tea company has accomplished. We were staying in Galle and it was a short drive through the beautiful countryside to the plantation. Some chose to go there by tuk-tuk, so it's not too far. You'll see some wild life getting there but so much more in the plantation - particularly birds. Monkeys were also there during our visit. Comfortable walking shoes would be wiseAlthough you are encouraged to taste test around 30 different teas (for free) there is no pressure to by anything, although you can. We brought home some of the tastiest tea we have ever had. We met a Sri Lankan man in Koggala who has lived in England for many years. He travels to Sri Lanka every year to visit family and buys a years supply of tea from this plantation before returning home. Yes it's that good.
title: Interesting tour, tea tasting and beautiful grounds

body: At Handunugoda you can learn the history of the White Tea, understand the special care that is needed to harvest the leafs. stroll through the entire manufacturing process of the tea, taste different kinds of teas and take home a remarkable souvenir of the country. A complete experience
title: History, culture and refined taste

body: Unfortunately we were sold a "bill of goods" by tour agency that we could visit both tea plantation and The Dutch Fortress in 6 hours from Colombo. The plantation is easily 2 to 2 1/2 hours from the city (we left port area at 6:30 am). I agree with another reviewers that staff is incredible friendly and that the tea served was excellent (if not pricey compared to shops in the city). Also disappointed that we did not see workers actually in fields with famed "virgin white tea". Supposedly never touched by human hands.
title: Long ride from Colombo

body: Very close to Ahangama this tea estate is situated, where we dropped by unannounced.A guide was readily available and showed us for free, what is growing at their estate, which was more than only tea. Something I did not expected.He showed us the black pepper, coffee bean plant, rubber trees and cinnamon tree. And explained how it was harvested in good English.Then we got some tea with chocolate cake, which my kids loved. I bearly managed to eat my own piece...A shame that they do not sell it!The small factory looked authentic en clean. Off course the free tour ended in a little shop where one could taste all the blends available. Even though the prices were high (higher than back home), we bought one package of tea and cinnamon to clear our guilt of enjoying a free tour.
title: Nice free educational tour

body: A really nice way to spend a morning or afternoon. Take the kids, they will have a blast picking flowers and running through the grounds.
title: Lovely tour and beautiful grounds

body: We loved this place. Peaceful and beautiful, lovely staff and great tasting tea. The courteous staff give you a tour of the estate, tea bushes and manufacturing; you then taste some tea and eat some chocolate cake. The surroundings are really beautiful and the story of Virgin White Tea really is a lovely one.There is a lovely shop with all of the teas and there is no pressure to buy at all. Of course you do though.We arranged a private driver to take us here from Ahungalla area which was perfect as it would be a little tricky finding this place alone.Wonderful day though, wonderful place.
title: Wonderful tea plantation!

body: Our tour guide was extremely knowledgeable and friendly.The tour is free and includes a short walk around the plantation to see the variety of tea growing on site, a delicious tea and chocolate cake break, visit to the production factory and ends with a tasting session of each tea produced. The tour isn’t very long in duration but gives you a detailed overview of the tea production process In the shop you can buy all the teas produced on site including the very rare Virgin White tea
title: Excellent free tour

body: My and my girlfriend were impressed by the tour. With all the interesting information, the cake and the tea tasting it was an outstanding experience. The tour is tip based wich we were more than happy to give!
title: A wonderful experience in the tea plantation

body: This is a very picturesque family run plantation. The guy running the tours is a real character! It was very interesting to see the process of tea being made, and the antique machines.
title: Definitely worth a visit

body: Lovely place. The guide is very cheerful and also ready to give any explanation. After you have a brief tea information and get a taste of many different tea!
