They also have tea available for selling and I’d suggest you to leave a tip in their tea room box. As this attraction is free of charge and they do make a good effort to serve you.
title: Worth visiting

body: We loved this place.We were lucky enough to get a very personal tour and insight into the estate as well as the tea making process.Felt very colonial to be sipping tea and eating chocolate cake outside a planters bungalow in an absolute downpour.The guide sorted out brollies for us and then we explored the very real delights of the original tea factory which due to its age is more like a working museum.it was great especially with the pouring rain teeming down on the corrugated roof felt very atmospheric.Great tour really interesting and learned a lot while getting drenched.
title: A trip back in time

body: We had a stop here on our way back to the airport. It was really a nice stop. Tour with a guide around the tea plantation was interesting. We also got to see the tea factory and also the taste different types of tea. The best of all: everything for free!
title: Interesting

body: We spent the morning at the tea plantation loved the tea and learning about tea growing and processing
title: Wonderfull Tea as it should be

body: I really enjoyed our visit to this tea estate. It’s what I pictured a visit to a tea estate should be like - complete with a lovely cup of oolong tea with a small piece of cake under a verandah mid-tour. Our guide was very knowledgeable and sweet, the setting was beautiful, a great way to spend an hour or two.
title: Tea fix

body: I took my English Composition students from the Galle and Matara branches of The American College of Higher Education for a writing assignment, and the overall experience was wonderful. All of the staff were amazingly polite and helpful, as well as the management who treated us to a personal tour of everything. The General Manager David Manickam was especially kind, making this experience one we will all remember!
title: Thoroughly Enjoyable

body: We had a wet afternoon in Unawatuna so took a tuktuk to handunugoda. Thoroughly enjoyed it. A free tour that lasted an hour or so including being served tea and cake and having a guide explain the process of tea making and show us the plants and machinery used, as well as coffee plants, cinnamon trees and rubber trees. At the end we were able to taste 30 different types of tea and could buy any ones we liked. Some of the teas were pricey to buy but we bought a box of one we liked the taste of which cost us 750rupees, we considered it a donation for the tour that we enjoyed. There was no pressure to buy or tip
title: Well worth a visit

body: We enjoyed our tour of this Tea Estate. It is small so it doesn't take very long but it was very pleasant. We loved seeing the 150 year machiniery still working. We did buy some tea but never felt under any pressure to do so.
title: Interesting & nice visit.

body: Our family enjoyed the complimentary tour of the plantation and factory, it was very interesting to see the process and was of course great to try the different teas at the end of the tour! Also thought it was a nice touch that they gave us chocolate cake and sapphire oolong tea on the porch.Also worth mentioning there wasn't any pressure to buy any tea or other merchandise at the end of the tour.
title: Enjoyable and educational

body: Great teas but expensive and a bit of a tourist trap where drivers drop busloads of people off and encourage purchases for commission.
title: Nice tea but a bit of a tourist trap

body: Brilliant to see all the stages of tea production - well worth a visit!.... You also get tea and cake!
title: Great tea plantation

body: Traveled out with tuc tuc from Fortress Resort for couple of hours. (1500-1800 rupees)Very interesting and enjoyable explanation of tea process and reasonably priced, good quality tea selection to buy.
title: Lovely trip for afternoon tea, village mini-tour and beautiful tea plantation

body: I had no idea there were so many different types of tea. The factory was very interesting. It was quite educational to see how they process the tea. They have a little store where you can taste all the teas and buy the ones you like. It was a very beautiful tea plantation. I also liked seeing the rubber trees and feel the sap.
title: Very informative

body: This is a free guide around a tea plantation. They take you around in groups and explain the processes. We had a cup of tea and chocolate cake which was Devine. The factory was very interesting and informative. The tea tasting and shop was great with no pressure to buy or leave a voluntary tip which goes into a box to be shared by all who work there. Well worth a visit.
title: Morning Trip

body: Informative and funny guide.No entrance fee and no pressure to buy.Cool little gift shop with loads of teas lined up.Also, the tuk tuk driver who took us waited for us.
title: Lovely Stuff!

body: This was a great place to learn about the tea industry and sample the goods. We were treated respectfully and got all of our questions answered. The tour itself was free, as were the samples and some delicious chocolate cake, and we spent a bunch on amazing teas to take home. Highly recommend!
title: Informative and free!

body: We rent scooters in Unawatuna for a day and visited this factory in the morning. Short walk with an experienced quide who takes you through the plantation to have a nice cup of tea and cake on the porch of an old house at the top of plantation. But don't expect any spectacular views. For those you must visit the central highlands (Nuwara Eliya, Haputale, Ella). Machines in the factory weren't working. Production of white tea is shown just on tv on the tea center. In the tea center we finally had very nice tea tasting (around 30 samples) and that was what were were looking for. Prices for the tea are much higher than in the north. Worth visit if you haven't been to any other plantation.
title: Best tea tasting

body: We had an excellent tour of the estate with a very friendly and funny guide! He was super knowledgeable and always brought the information back to us with a personal connection--like tea's importance to America's independence etc. he even had a little book with common phrases in various languages so he could make all of his guests feel at home/comfortable! I was shocked that there wasn't more pressure to buy things at the end of the tour considering they gave us free tea and cake in the middle of it! Wish they had more small packets of tea or even a sampler pack in the shop to buy instead of the larger quantities of a single type of tea! Overall this was an awesome relaxing and informative little half day trip from Mirissa and I would recommend it to anyone in the area looking for something other than beach related activities to fill a day!
title: Super tour guide!

body: Great short day trip if you are staying in the Ahangama area.. a brief tour through then plantation a complementary cup of tea and cake, quick peek at the machinery, then the opportunity to sample countless varieties of tea and select your favourites if you wish to buy.
title: Family day out with parents

body: Knowledgeable guide explains the tea plantation and how it’s collected. You get served a free tea an piece of cake. You proceed to the factory where you are shown how to get from fresh cut plants/leaves to the tea as you know it. You see the old machin while they work, it’s really interesting. You finish at a shop were you can taste the different varieties and get no pressure to buy though you most definitely want to get some !
title: Great visit

body: We have been here today and I could not wish for better explanation about the whole process of making tea from collecting the leaves to drying and packing the tea. We had a beautiful walk through the gardens and we could taste different kind of teas and buy them at the shop. It was really nice and edifying. Thanks
title: Amazing tea tasting and walk through the whole tea factory

body: An experienced guide tells the story of tea planting, cultivation and harvesting with humor and detail on a walk through the plantings. He graciously answers questions as you sip a cup on the garden terrace. Next a second guide narrates the process of withering, rolling, fermenting, grading and selling. Employees are operating the machines as you walk through the factory. Finally you enter the tasting room for an opportunity to sample teas grown in many areas of Sri Lanka. Shelves are stocked with attractively packaged boxes of all the teas so you can purchase your favorites.
title: Tea explained, also sipped, sampled and sold at Handunugoda Tea Estate

body: Very well run tour with obvious emphasis on tea, but also on spices that grow on the property. They also have a nice store where you can buy a large variety of teas as well as books on the history and cultivation of tea leaves.
title: Tea and spice tour

body: Great tour, entertaining guide, beautiful tea plantation. Free of charge and includes tea and cake at the house. Fabulous!
title: Lovely tea plantation

body: We were only at the beach in Sri Lanka on holiday with the family but I really wanted to visit a tea estate. Fortunately our villa manager organised a visit for us to the Handugoda Tea Estate and this proved to be excellent. We were taken on a nice short walking tour through the tea plantations and then served tea and cake in a beautiful old colonial house in the estate. This was followed by a guided visit to the factory and then to the shop. There was no charge for the visit other than a request for a tip for the staff and the opportunity to shop int he store. It was a wonderful visit which we really enjoyed.
title: Wonderful tour of the tea estate and factory

body: We recently visited this tea plantation. We had a tour of the plants, then we had a cup of tea with chocolate cake before seeing the factory process. Very interesting and there was no hard sell or pressure to buy the tea. Worth a visit if your in the area.
title: Fascinating

body: A short tea tour around this beautiful estate is a nice attraction. The degustation of tea with the cake is probably the best part. It is comfortable to taste various teas in the selling room. Prices are quite high even for ordinary brands.
title: Picturesque tea estate

body: An interesting hour or so at the tea factory learning about how tea is produced. Free entry and no hard sell at the gift shop so a pleasant experience overall.
title: see how tea is made

body: We found this trip via trip advisor and glad we did! From kottawa we took a tuktuk to the plantation. We were welcomed by the guide who gave us a tour of the tea growing and the production plant. We also could try some tea and cake in the lovely tea house. In addition to tea, he also showed us the rubber, cinnamon, coffee and peppercorn plants growing on the plantation. Everything was free and the tipping is restricted to a box at the end which is shared between all staff. The shop at the end sells tea produced at the plantation
title: Beautiful setting and good way to fill an hour or so

body: This place seems to be set up for tourists, which doesn't make it worthless, just predictable. You can see the different tea plants, rubber plants, cinnamon, and many other types of plants.Tour guide was good, got to walk around the plants, then the factory, drink some tea and then the shop at the end. Honestly an enjoyable 1+ hours.If you're in the area, go.BTW, white tea is expensive!
title: good tour

body: We stopped into to this estate on the drive through to Galle, and were pleasantly surprised at this quirky little establishment. While we were never really sure what was going on, we were served a lovely afternoon tea (tea and cake, at no cost), followed by a tour of the gardens and tea factory, and then a tasting of over 20 different house-made teas.We had the most unique tour guide, whose school-master type persona somehow led to us having a great time throughout the tour.While it’s a little off the main drag, and not as entirely informative as other more generic plantation tours, it was certainly a worthwhile detour.
title: Quirky little tea factory

body: Meril our tour guide was very kind and knowledgable.Herman was the plantation owner and mentioned its been in the family for 120 years as cocunut and rubber plantation. They still produce rubber. It comes as a sap from a tree in white colour. Herman turned this into tea plantation for only last 25 years.Its the only tea plantation that produces virgin white tea. I did notice cheaper priced teas in hikkaduwa stores. About half the price so maybe 900SLR for 100grs. Vs 300 SLR for 100grs. Not sure what the shop qualities were as I'm not a tea conisure but buying at the plantation ensures direct pay for the staffs hard work.Definitely a must do while in Sri Lanka. Plenty of plantations around but avoid the touristic ones. Note that they all have early closing times so be sure to arrange based on the hours of operation for the plantation you chose to go to.
title: Beautiful. Friendly staff. Variety of teas.

body: The drive there was the most interesting bit. We got there and were told to join a group that had done most of the tour. We saw rubber trees, coffee trees and pepper trees, little to none explanation, then got taken to a tea terrace to taste their sapphire tea and choc cake which was ok. Then we asked to join another group to actually hear about the tea plants themselves, this lasted for about 7 minutes, to which then we joined yet another group to go to the final stage of seeing the machinery which was interesting and then off to the shop. Relatively overpriced tea although it does look quite labour intensive. All in all you need 30 minutes and good luck to get a good guide. I would recommend it only if you are really into tea or maybe try another plantation, not much effort put into this. I know this is a free service and that’s great, however I wouldn’t mind paying for a more organised and insightful tour.
title: Average

body: Our driver was a bit surprised we wanted to go here. He had never heard of the place and was very curious how we learned about it (thanks tripadvisor). The whole experience was great. Our guide spoke very good English and was very knowledgable. We got to see not only tea plants but also coffee, rubber, pepper and hibiscus. After walking a bit through the estate we stop at a tea house for a free sample of tea and chocolate cake. Both were very good. We then headed to the manufacturing area. It was really interesting to see how they dry the leaves, separate and grade the leaves. Most of the machines seemed to be very old machines from colonial times. Finally our tour ended at the store. There was no pressure to buy tea (but we did). The store had samples available for tasting of all the different varieties. Overall it was a great experience that both kids and adults found interesting.
title: Very informative and interesting tour

body: As we had planned a trip to Nuwara Eliya for later in our travel itinerary, we were uncertain about whether to also visit this tea plantation. We are so pleased that we did go! It was fantastic!! The tour guide was very knowledgeable and friendly and we were shown all the plants grown on the plantation including white tea, cinnamon, pepper and coffee. The tour included a complimentary tasting of sapphire Oolong tea and chocolate cake on the beautiful verandah. The tour culminated in the tea processing factory and we were shown the drying, sorting and processing of the res leaves. The highlight of this visit was the colourful tropical plants and lush scenery as well as the serenity of the countryside. I would highly recommend a visit.
title: Fantastic and unexpected delight hidden in the lush countryside!

body: Knowledgable guides and exquisite setting (esp. the quaint manor house on the hill which we visited for a slice of cold cake and a cup of white tea). Groves of tea hemmed by colourful flowering bushes and trees. Both the tour of the estate and the tea tasting is free (a welcome touch). We bought the book 'The suicide club' written by the plantation-owner and are finding it an enjoyable read. He is quite a card. We also purchased some of the tea after the tasting, for gifting. A tuk tuk driver was willing to take us to the plantation from Ahangama for 600 rupees return. A highlight for us.
title: Rewarding tour of established tea estate with high tea in colonial setting

body: We enjoyed our visit, very well done. Of course it is geared towards tourists, but you don't feel scammed, there is true pride in the people who show you around.Asides from tea you also see rubber, cinnamon and pepper trees.The tea tasting is fun as well. Ok, the prices at the shop are anything but bargain, but we didn't mind paying a little more for the experience, also, there was no pressure.
title: Now we know how tea is made, well done!

body: A great option for experiencing a tea plantation close to Galle. You get a tour of the plantation and to see how tea, rubber and cinnamon are grown and harvested. There’s also a chance to sample a wide range of teas in a lovely tasting room at the end.
title: Informative, friendly and well worth a visit

body: What a great informative visit. It takes you through history it the tea story and how it started out in Sri Lanka. Very very informative guides who spoke really good English. An opportunity to taste all the different teas produced at the plantation so you can take one home to your liking rather than guess. I will definitely recommend a visit to here.
title: Tea tour

body: It was a great experience. I went with my family (there are 8 of us) and we were provided with a brilliant tour from Romesh, our guide. We received a cup of tea grown at the plantation and a slice of cake. You are also able to buy some of the teas and the signature 'white tea' at the shop at the end of the tour. We all had a good time.
title: Informative and Interesting

body: We arrived here via tuk tuk from Unawatuna - easy journey took about 30 minutes. We were ushered straight into a small group for a tour around the tea plantation by a localguide who spoke great English. Complimentary Oolong tea and chocolate cake were served before moving onto the factory to see how the tea is produced. Finished at their on site shop where a variety of teas and products are available. Absolutely no pressure to buy and no fee for the tour - a communal tip jar is available. An interesting couple of hours overall!
title: Informative tour

body: Really interesting tour.Not only tea but rubber, cinnamon & coffee.Never realised there were so many tea flavours.The factory still used the original machinery over 145 years old.The tasting is fantastic.
title: Interesting & surprising.

body: This is huge plantation where they harvest tea, rubber, pepper and cinnamon. There is no cost for the tour. There is a shop where you can taste all the different types of tea. There is no pressure to buy. Our guide Xavier explained in detail the process of how tea is made. Along the tour he showed us how rubber is extracted from the trees and showed us the cinnamon trees and pepper vines. The explanation of how white tea is harvested is fascinating.
title: Informative Tea Tour

body: The ancient machines of this plantation provide you with insight to the history of tea and the Island which calls it it's National drink. The 2 hour tour is beautiful as it meanders around the plantations and the factory. You can buy a huge variety of local teas after your morning or afternoon tea in the Plantation House.
title: History of Sri Lanka in Tea

body: We had ventured out from our hotel on a tuc tuc tour and our driver took us to this tea plantation and factory as one stop on our mornings ride. We were mixed with a number of other Europeans and guided by a wizened Sri Lankan gentleman with a wicked sense of humour. My understanding of tea and how it is grown and prepared for sale is almost 100 per cent greater for this tour. There is plenty of time to look around the plantation and not just at tea plants. There is a lovely stop for tea and cake before visiting the factory. It is astonishing to see some of the old equipment still working today. You finish off with a great tea tasting and the chance to buy some home grown and produced tea and there is no pressure to buy. The tour was made memorable by the banter between our guide and the members of our group. Expect to take 1.5 hours for the whole experience. Brilliant!!
title: Brilliant and a bloody good laugh!

body: Virgin white tea plantation Here they harvest rubber, tea and cinnamon No charge for entry you give a donation on exit A guide took us round explaining about the teas showed us how the tea was picked, harvested and manufactured into tea Very interesting We tried different teas to help us choose what we wanted to buy They take visa, that have toilets and we we're given a cup of tea and a piece of cake Worth looking around and very interesting
title: Great tour

body: Our guide Xavier was well informed and spoke several languages.He provided us with an insightful tour of the tea estate, interspersed with some humour. We learned a great deal more than expected about the making of tea and the resilience of the machinery still operating today to sort the tea. Some fascinating information. The white tea did taste wonderful. The hard sell at the end was a little overwhelming and did dampen the overall experience. Still worth while and we bought a few spices to use on our return home.
title: Great insight into the work that goes into a simple cup of tea.

body: It was interesting to see coffee, cinnamon, pepper and several types of tea growing. Our tour guide was very informative. We hiked up a hill looking at plants all the way and were served a cup of tea at the top. We went back down and saw how different types of tea are processed. Some of the equipment is about 150 years old and still functioning!At the end of the tour you could taste all the teas they produce there. There was a short film too.The tour was free. While there is no pressure to buy tea, the cost of the tea was not known until checkout and seems to have the cost of the tour built into it.
title: Wide variety of plants

body: We spent a few hours here as part of a bigger tour and really enjoyed, the plantation itself is beautiful with lots more to see than just tea , there is a lovely house where they serve you tea and cake on the veranda , a tour of the factory and then a museum , all in all a very interesting and enjoyable few hours
title: Really enjoyable trip

body: This was a educational tour- got to learn a lot about the tea process from picking to processing. The visit is free of charge.It’s free to go to & the guide we had was excellent & really knowledgeable.There is tea tasting & cake to enjoy.There is a tea shop - which to be honest I thought was overpriced given you are buying from the source.There is also a tip box in the shop - but this is at your discretion & there is no pressure to buy the tea or to tip
title: Good overview of tea process

body: I wanted to visit a tea plantation but was worried about being in the south and not finding a good one...oh I was wrong! This place is wonderful. I was met by a smiling funny guide who walked me round the different tea areas and explained how the infusion process worked. He showed me the virgin white tea bushes (no touching) and then we sat and went through all the types of tea they produce whilst supping a lovely cuppa with a nice slice of chocolate cake made by a very shy lady. I then was shown the still working machines in the factory (some from the late 1800’s) and learnt about the way the tips/leaves are turned into loose and bagged tea. I liked how they use both heavy old industrial methods alongside modern tech and the good old human hand! The shop is brilliant, a tea drinkers paradise with at least 40 to try and buy. I must mention my guides sense of humour! When, in my usual fashion, I questioned whether the ladies who worked on the virgin white section of the plantation still had to follow the Chinese tradition of remaining virgins whilst trimming the bushes he laughed...’no sir, I don’t think we would be able to harvest the tips if that was still the case’ Legend ! Lovely place, thoroughly recommended!
title: A fun and informative visit

body: We planned to make quick stop, to at least have seen it. So wrong we planned...It started with the background and the story behind the virgin white tea. Very interesting and honest. Then we went for a short walk; smelled fresh cinnamon, saw rubber, pepper before we ended up in a little cute tea house. Here we were served delicious tea with chocolate cake! We continued to walk to the tea factory where our guide explained the manufacturing process to produce tea, so interesting! Machines still working for 145 years, it’s like walking in a live museum.After the factory we stopped at the gift shop in which we could taste all different kind of teas, so nice!All this for no cost! We put a tip in the gift shop as that was the option given to us.Highly recommend to make visit here!
title: Fantastic visit!

body: I searched tea plantations around Sri Lanka before I went and this place caught my eye due to the reviews so I waited until we got to Hikkaduwa and we decided to make a trip up as it would be very un Sri Lankan to not visit a tea plantation. Our expectations were certainly met. We were greeted with a pot of tea and some cake surrounded by the most lush green surroundings in the middle of tea fields this was for free. It was amazing. We did the tea tour as well which was also for free and very informative. After the tour we went into the tea museum and tried all their teas. I ended up purchasing quite a few teas and gave them a well deserved tip for their incredible hospitality. I highly recommend holding off on other tea plantations which are more commercialized as this was well worth it.
title: Highly recommend

body: We were taken on tour by the plantation manager. Very informing and interesting. Half way through the short tour, we were taken to a house where we were served a cup of tea (ours happened to be oolong that day) and a piece of chocolate cake! Mind you, that is called service when the tour is free of charge. There's also tea tasting in the tea shop. You can sample their 40 varieties available for sale. My 6yo son enjoyed this part the most...tasting all the teas. The tea for sale is a bit on the pricey side. There are signs that say the staff do not take individual tips and to put it in the donation box.
title: Pleasant visit

body: This is a small, multi-crop estate with rubber, cinnamon, black-pepper and the black and white teas.Great tour guides who do a fair job of explaining the tea cultivation and manufacturing process.The tasting eliminates the need for a hard-sell. The quality of the product ensures that you end up buying your favorite teas from here
title: Interesting tour/ tea tasting

body: Really enjoyable visit! Saw tea, coffee, peppercorns, rubber and pineapples growing. Guide was friendly and explained everything well. Free cup of tea and chocolate cake was very nice. Then visited the factory and saw the process the tea goes through before tea tasting in the shop. There was no pressure to buy anything in the shop and the guides don't accept tips, there is a box in the shop if you want to tip but you don't have to - we did as the guide was great and as a thank you for the tea and cake. Well worth visiting, highly recommended!!
title: Great visit

body: This is a wonderful organic tea plantation that had been in the same family for 140 years. The tour is fascinating and free with tea and cake and a tea tasting at the end. The equipment is old and beautiful - one machine was made by the same Irish company that built the Titanic. There is no pressure to buy with a communal tip box if you want to.
title: Go there!

body: If, like us, you want to explore the inland part of the southern coastal strip then do visit here as you will learn a great deal about the production of tea, plus be offered a great cuppa and a slice of cake. Don't believe that you have to enter hill country to experience exceptional tea.
title: A good introduction to the workings of a tea factory

body: If you're wanting to visit a tea plantation in the south this is worth a trip. They were very informative, had a country feel, tea and cake. Make sure you too though as you leave to help them as there is no cover charge for the entry. I love tea so I purchased my favourites. It's good understanding he process and seeing the different plants and trees here in Sri Lanka. Beware of tuk-tuk drivers taking you elsewhere.....avoid the herb gardens as they are a scam!
title: Very nice Tea Plantation

body: Absolute must visit. Takes about an hour to do a tour. They do not accept individual tipping which is nice. A good tour, full of historic information. Beautiful scenery. The factory tour was exceptional. Up close to the machinery. Get to touch the tea. At the end there are all 40 teas to taste. They use the lemongrass, ginger and cinnamon on the property to make their teas. Nothing goes to waste. I'm a beer drinker and this tour of tea was excellent. Of the 3 tea factories we visited this was by far the best and the cheapest!!! The others were way to busy (even in off season) and take advantage of tourists / customers. Handunugoda is genuine great tea and a great tour experience. Loved it.!
title: Best Tea Estate in SRI LANKA

body: We wanted to see how they produce the tea here in Sri Lanka, we were recommended to go fram Galle to Handunugoda Tea Estate, and we were not disappointed. A nice tuktuk ride to get there with lovely scenery and a hord of water buffalos in the middle of the road. At the estate we were greeted by our very knowledgable guide who showed us around the different plants and specifically the virgin white plan that is what they are most famous for. mid-tour we were served cake and tea and after the tour we got to try the whole range of teas, including the very exclusive "virgin white tea" all free of charge. I would highly recommend a visit to this lovely little place!
title: Hot day at the tea estate

body: We visited this small tea plantation as we had read good reviews about it. It was a three quarters of an hour tuk-tuk ride from Galle and the journey itself was interesting as we took the Matara Road which follows the coast. En route you are able to see the stilt fishermen at Welligama as well as the beautiful beach Mirissa.The tea plantation was really interesting. We were shown around by a member of staff who pointed out the different teas as well as different trees (cinnamon for example). We were served tea and cake. At the end of the tour you are given a short talk by the owner and encouraged to sample as many of the teas on display as you would like.You do not need to book for this tour which is completely free. It passes a very nice hour or two, particularly if like us you are in the middle of a tropical downpour. Go! You won't be disappointed
title: Tea time!

body: This is definitely worth a visit. We learned about so many of the different plants growing on the state, including rubber trees and breadfruit. There is no hassle to buy anything, just a comfortable, enjoyable free tour with tea and coffee included. Well worth a visit!
title: Informative free tour and tea tasting

body: We really enjoyed the tour looking at different plants but once we got to the shop the man got the hump because we wouldn't buy anything.
title: Hard sell

body: Fabulous tea plantation & factory and off the beaten track so even better as you see even more of very rural Sri Lanka.Super tour of the estate, explanations of the different tea plants, also rubber, black pepper, coffee, lemongrass, jackfruit... Tea and cake on the terrace at the owner's villa felt very special followed by an incredibly interesting tour of the working factory and then tea tasting of 40 amazingly different varieties including Silver Tips, Golden Tips and Hundungoda's exclusive and exquisite Virgin White Tea. Highly recommend this Tea Plantation !
title: Excellent Tea Estate

body: Visited in July and had a great couple of hours at the plantation. The tour is free and you are taken for about half and hour through the plantation to see the plants, then to the house for tea and cake. You then visit the factory and can watch 150 year old machinery in action.The last stop is the tea and gift shop where ladies will prepare over 40 different teas for you to try. All teas are for sale but there is no pressure to buy any. There is also a donation box as you leave because the whole tour is free!! Definitely worth the journey from town.
title: Excellent plantation tour and tea tasting!

body: My friends and I wanted to learn more about the virgin White tea so we thought we'd head by the Estate. We were pleasantly surprised by the free tour of the plantations and factory, and even more so of the tea tasting (from which we left light-headed from all the side-effects).
title: Fantastic Tea Tour

body: Not too far off the main highway heading south from Colombo. Informative tour of the plantation that focuses not just on tea. Complimentary tea on the verandah of the homestead and of course a tour of the factory - wow!!Massive selection of teas to try at the shop. Worthwhile visit
title: Informative visit - lovely place

body: Getting to this plantation alone is an experience. We encountered a herd of water buffalo, which was really fun. Our host, David, was great and met us at our car. He explained everything that they grow there in addition to the tea. It was a really fascinating and it was a nice and tranquil walk around the grounds. The tea and cakes at the house were memorable including meeting their two dogs. Seeing the old original machinery in action was really neat. I had no idea what went in to creating tea from start to finish and it was really fun to learn. Of course, we couldn't leave without some cinnamon, pepper, and tea. This was definitely a highlight of my time in Galle.
title: Worth a visit

body: We visited here as part of our room package at the Amangalla in GalleFort.It was a delightful few hours with David from the tea plantation regaling stories from yesteryear and more recent times. He was great company.My teenage daughter was enthralled by the stories of the beginnings and history of the expensive virgin white tea. We bought some of the special white tea - who can resist with anti-aging properties and such strong anti-oxidants and a lovely taste to boot.The tea and chocolate cake were all perfect served on the terrace of the old manor house. This is a must visit when in Galle.
title: A great experience

body: The tour is free and the guide gives you a good overview of the different plants and the tea making process. You are given a cup of tea and a piece of cake and the guide tells you to tip the lady who serves it. Although there is a notice at the beginning of the tour telling you not to tip individuals, but to leave a tip in the box to be shared. There is plenty of tea for sale, although it is not cheap.
title: Interesting Tour

body: Really interesting, see how the tea is made in the factory, hear about how they make cinnamon, rubber, coffee and black pepper. You stop for a taste of tea and cake which they politely ask you to tip for so as a warning be ready for that. It was a very quiet time of year and we felt that they pressured us quite a bit to buy more tea, we bought some and they seemed disappointed. Still we found it very interesting.
title: Very Interesting

body: Our family is very passionate about tea and this is one of the reasons why we chose Sri Lanka as our family holiday destination. The visit to this lovely tea plantation is worth it... seeing everything from tea cultivation all the way to the harvest and production. The tea plantation in itself is not postcard pretty and the whole estate could benefit from a series of renovations here and there but take away the facade and you are embraced by a unique tea heritage that will blow you away and give you a much higher respect to every sip that you take out of any tea they produce.The white tea of course was the star of the show. It is the most expensive they have and worth every drop and sip. You are given a free tasting of their 40+ tea variations so you will have an afternoon of beating your head if you should buy half of the estate or not. But if you have but one tea to choose, let it be the white tea... Very subtle and poignant and poetic in every layer you can savor.We also loved the Suicide Club blend, which is a unique blend with hints of brandy and also has an interesting story behind its rather unusual name!Do yourself a favor and find this little treasure.
title: One of the highlights of our Sri Lanka holiday!

body: You must visit this place for tea and cake, lovely area quite deep in the jungle. Joseph our guide was very good, funny and great english.
title: Hidden Gem

body: Gorgeous and calm tea estate where the staff gives you a free tour of the factory and the whole estate. The machines are almost 150 years old but it's very intricate how they separate the leaves etc. Also, a great way to take a break from all the beach activities.
title: Beautiful Tea Estate

body: It was a rainy afternoon so we decided to venture to the Tea Estate, we didn't really know what to expect, but it was a fantastic afternoon. Free to enter and just need to tip at the end.
title: Great way to spend an afternoon

body: We had a really great time there. The guide was very informative and the tea was fresh and tasty!!! Don't miss it if you're in Tangalle.
title: Worth Visiting!

body: A short wander through the plants with a guide showing and explaining how they farm. We saw peppercorns, coffee, latex, hibiscus, mango, parakeets, a Labrador and a Golden Retriever, beautiful flowers I can't name and many many tea bushes. Then tea with chocolate cake before a short stroll to the 'machineries' where the tea making process was underway. Final stop was the museum, the room you see in their photo where you are able to taste as many or few teas as you like. We bought their namesake the White Tea which was simply delicious. Take cash, no cards accepted. Our excursion was organised through our hotel Tri, on Lake Koggala which was a jolly 20 minute Tuk Tuk ride away. A fun outing - even the teens liked it.
title: Short and sweet

body: Well worth a visit! Great getting to have a little cup to sample! Really good guides although 40mins is another to view it
title: Good visit

body: We visited the plantation on the Sri Lankan new year's eve so the factory wasn't open because of the holidays. Still got a nice tour with a expert guide, nice tea tasting with cake and in the shop we tasted about 40 different teas. It was nice to see where the tea is grown and that it is produced in ecological and ethical way.
title: A lush tea plantation

body: Accidentally I have to visit this place.But it was fortunate....Situated near Galle. Have to travel Galle Matara rd towards Matara and turn left from Ahangama junction towards Hiniduma rd....Then you get the direction.This is medium size family own business.Very well organize estate...You Will get shorter estate tour with explaining about tea and some spice ,Tea process and factory.It's good experience and it's only few tea factory in down south to visits travelers.
title: Down south TEA

body: We have visited this plantation during our stay in Kabalana. Overall very nice experience. You can see how the tea is made using machines that are very old sometimes. There is a great selection of teas in the store and you can taste all of them before you choose what to buy. There is also a short walk through the plantation that is explaining how it works. There are no extremely fantastic views there if you are looking for any. Overall if you are in South Srilanka, near Kabalana it is a good idea for afternoon trip.
title: Very nice tea plantation

body: We have visited several tea plantations in Elle region but this place is absolutelly different. The guided tours are interesting and tea degustation is for free. Perfect oportunity to taste more than 20 kinds of tea and to buy some unique. Highly recommended.
title: Different kind of tea plantation

body: Its nice to learn something about the virgin white tea, taste it and have a piece of cake. After visit you can buy some tea if interested. But its all for free - not a common thing at Srí Lanka.
title: Worth visiting

body: Basic tea plantation tour. Best part was seeing the processing equipment and how it runs. They try to make the tour last 2 hours... 30 minutes is more than enough!
title: Very basic tea plantation tour

body: This is a small privately owned tea factory and plantation. The tour, including the guide, is free. After walking around the gardens for a while looking not just at tea but also coffee, pepper and cinnamon you are given a free cup of tea with cake. Next to the factory where the entire drying and preparation process is explained. Most of the machinery which is used is 145 years old and so it is like a working museum. Then to the tasting room where you have the opportunity to taste 29 different teas. Tasting notes are available in many different languages. At this stage you have the opportunity to buy some of the teas. Our guide did not have good English and the tour would have rated top marks if we had been able to get better answers to questions.
title: Interesting tea tasting experience

body: Hnadunugoda is the best low country tea tour one cold have in a tea estate, factory and tea tasting facility.Extremely tourist friendly place and most importantly its the only one in Sri lanka and one of few factories that produced white Tea which is very expensive and completely human untouched manufacturing process. it also produce various oolong tea products.
title: Best low country Tea tour ( White Tea and Oolong tea producer) , a must for Tea lovers

body: It was interesting to hear about the different teas and spices they use in tea, but the most interesting was about white tea. The tour is not too long and you finish off see how the tea is dried and cleaned followed by a tea tasting of all the varieties they produce.
title: Informative

body: We had a nice visit here. The tour of the grounds was pleasant and the tour of the plant was very educational. Prices in the salon were a bit pricey but it was great to try different teas. We had a very nice host.
title: Nice diversion from the beach

body: Fairly nice thing to do near koggala, with free entry. Our tour guide was quite fed up and didn't have a lot of enthusiasm, but it was nice that it was only us on the tour. The shop is fairly expensive and they ask you to tip the tea pourer. Really enjoyed the chance to taste the tea range, worth going if just for that.
title: Quiet grounds but I've been to better tea plantations

body: Enjoyed the rural drive up there by tuktuk. Entrance free and you can taste lots of teas and have a slice of cake! The tour was interesting , seeing and hearing all about the process. We also visited the factory, where some of the machinery is 150 years old.Finished with a visit to the shop (!) but no real pressure to buy.
title: Low land tea estate

body: A good trip for half a day from the Galle area. Very easy to access by bus (just get on a bus going along the Galle-Matara road and get off at Kathaluwa railway station, then you can Tuk Tuk from the road easily). The guide was very friendly and knowledgeable, we got to try different teas and some cake and were able to stop at the factory too (but not enough time for taking photos!). Trying the tea at the end was the most exciting, so many different colours.Impressive that all of this was for free, and that there didn't feel like there was any obligation to buy anything, although plenty of opportunity to! I would say that look out for the donation box if you want to leave a donation because it is very small.
title: Interesting day out near Galle

body: After seeing the highland plantations near Nuwara Eliya, we wanted to see a lowland plantation. Handunogoda was more beautiful and we were given much more information about the tea processes and about other plants. Joseph, our guide was full of information and ttpook time to explain things and answer our questions. The tea and chocolate cake were delicious and we had a tea tasting session after visiting the factory. We met Herman Guneratne, the famous tea planter and were pleased to buy his book, The Suicide Club. The visit was one of the highlights of our trip.
title: A beautiful place

body: During the vocation we stayed in Koggala, so it was the only tea factory in our area. Excursion is free. It starts with a cup of tea and "brownie", than you walk with a English-speaking guide through the plantation to the factory. I can't say, that excursion is much informative, though you can make some lovely photos. The third step is tasting, where you can try all the types of tea, which are produced by the factory, and, of-course, you are suggested to buy some tea. The prices are starting from 750 rps for 30 gram up to 2500 rps for "virgin white tea". "True fans" of tea told me, that the real one grows only in the center of island (for ex. near Kandy), nevertheless, Handunugoda is good variant for those, who just want to spend time with pleasure, to make some photos and to buy some small presents for friends.
title: Nice place to visit

body: Lovely place with lots of history. Well worth a visit, never realised there were so many teas and to see the process from leaf to tea was very interesting
title: Lovely place

body: We visited Handunugoda Tea Estate some years ago and had a wonderful experience. The setting was exquisite and the guide very knowledgeable - from rubber production to virgin white tea.They were very accommodating of our small children. We still ship our tea from there and will be visiting them again in a few months time. Highly recommended.
title: I agree with all the excellent reviews

body: 1. Free of charges. 2. Offer free tasting of tea, including luxury white tea and a small piece of cake. 3. The guide did explain the tea plants, type of leaves, the factory operations in very details. Recommend anyone to go. We bought some tea box, including Virgin white tea. It was quite expensive. in some shops in Galle, we could find white tea as well. They were of much lower price. But, of course, they are of different brands.
title: Very informative guide tour

body: Very interesting visit, highly recommended. Not pushy on their sales, which is a relief in Sri Lanka.So glad we went, and would actually go again .Virgin White Tea is mega expensive , but we bought some anyway! Another 25 or so teas that you WILL taste, are modestly priced should you wish to buy.
title: Fascinating Experience and Free!

body: So many samples to try after a gentle stroll through the tea plantation with a humorous guide who was also very knowledgeable. Tea and cake supplied for just a donation. We were taken around the factory and the whole process of making tea was described. Low key, simple, wonderful trip in the sunshine.
title: Fascinating

body: Wonderful estate providing tea to luxury European tea brands.The visit started with a walk among the incredibly rich collection of bubbles plants of the plantation and explanations for each tea/tree variety.We were then welcomed at the owner's house for tea and homemade cake (both delicious) before following the visit of the factory and finally the tea shop (where tea is considerably less expensive than the same one sold in Europe!).Note: tea factory museum wasn't open yet but should open at some point in 2017.Highly recommended.
title: Enchanting tea plantation

body: Arrived at the plantation around 10 am, just in time to join the tour with a small family. Our guide was friendly and informative, the complimentary tea and cake were nice, though I would perhaps have preferred a more extensive walk around the plantation.The tour of the tea factory was very nice and interesting, learned a lot about making tea. The supervisor leading the tour knew his stuff, the old machines looked cool, even more so in action. The tea tasting was very nice as well. You get a small glass and a big spoon and then you can just scoop to your hearts delight from the 30 or so different teas that are available. Small thing, I realise it may be impractical, but it would be nice if the teas were served hot to better taste them. You can buy each tea in the shop, but they can get a bit expensive, think at least 1000 slr for 75 grams of tea, more for the more interesting teas. Haven't visited any other tea factories yet, so can't compare prices. If you don't want to buy tea, leaving a small tip in the box by the exit is also fine.
title: Nice tour, nice people, nice teas

body: Nice place. The gentleman giving us the tour was the Estate Manager of the property. He explained us nicely the tea-plantation and the tea-making process. Being an avid tea-drinker & lover, i really liked the whole tour and was excited to see the old British era machines still being used. To taste the Virgin White tea was really exciting and i loved the smooth and aromatic profile of the tea. You can also buy other tea-leaves or tea-bags of different quality from the estate/factory, though these are a bit expensive compared to outside market.
title: A good short visit on a lazy day

body: They offered a free excursion about how the tea, cinnamon, pepper grow and are collected. Then you will be offered tea tasting with cake. You can see the process of collecting tea and buy some tea.
title: Interesting excursion and plesant staff

body: This is a must see if you are in the area. Give it about 2 hours. This is free, but do accept (non pressured) donations. We had an excellent tour guide who was very informative. We had a scooter and made our trip from Marissa up the coast which was scenic for a good few miles! Lots of tea and some cake to try also!
title: A must see!

body: Tours of this tea plantation take under an hour. Our guide was very knowledgeable in explaining the types of tea grown, the differences between black and green varieties and how the famous white tea is made. Cake and sapphire oolong tea is served midway through the tour, free of charge, before a tour of the processing plant. Very interesting to see the tea leaves being dried, crushed, heated and sifted. The end of the tour takes you to a tasting room where you can try their 30+ varieties. I loved the Ruby oolong tea. White tea goes for over $55 AUD for a small batch and, despite the high antioxidant load, is otherwise an underperformer on taste (comparatively) , yet still clean and enjoyable. See what you think
title: Great tour of beautiful tea fields.

body: Free of charge excursion around the tea estate. You can see where the tea, cinnamon, pepper grow, how they are collected and packed. Afterwards visit the museum to try out different types of tea. Prices are above average, 1000-1500 per box, but they claim it is one of the finest. Total time at the estate: 1,5 hour
title: Quiet journey

body: nice and perfect , love to be in this place , there is nice nature which make my mind really calm , a
title: well perfect , love to be there

body: An informative and interesting visit to a working Tea plantation/tea production facility where we learned the process of tea-making from bud to cup. Really fascinating, and finished with a tasting session of over 20 teas!!The tour and tasting are free but you finish up with the tasting in the shop - be warned that you will probably be tempted to buy a LOT of tea as it tastes so good!Really fun tour, highly recommended.
title: Informative and fun!

body: You don't need more than a couple of hours to visit this small tea estate (it also grows pepper, Cinnamon and rubber) and can give you a flavour of Sri Lanka. After a short walk up the hill, where we were given a short talk, we stopped for a cup of tea and cake. We then had a tour around the factory before trying an buying some of the teas of the manufacturer. A restful way to spend the time
title: Enjoyable visit to this small estate

body: The source of the world's Virgin White tea. We had a very informative tour of the estate and factory with Shirley, who also has a great sense of humour. This is really a working museum - the same equipment from 145 years ago is being used to dry, crush and sort the tea.It's amazing how many different types of plants, herbs and teas are grown on this plantation - rubber trees, pepper, cinnamon, jasmine, aloe, etc. Shirley played a game with us and asked us to guess each plant that he would pluck a leaf from, based on the taste or smell. I got 0 out of 10..The tea and cake on the veranda was nice, and then we went into the tea tasting room. It's great to be able to taste before you buy and I loved all the colours of the tea - yellow, deep orange, red, green, etc..Donations are welcome in the shop and it's well worth it as the staff are very knowledgeable and friendly. Highly recommended stop for a couple of hours, about 30-40 mins from Galle.
title: A working tea museum/factory

body: We came here with Ransiri our Tuk Tuk driver (+94 71 636 2135) who was a great guide and a lovely guy.We arrived about 4pm and were a little rushed through the tour of the grounds. The complimentary tea was very nice and the factory tour was very interesting. Though, if you want to see the factory in action you will need to arrive before 2pm when work stops.Tasting the teas before buying was helpful and buying a few is recommended as the tour and tasting is free.
title: Quaint little place

body: Short ride from Galle, it is an all-in-one tea experience. From plantation to factory; teas tastings to tea shopping, we did it all in one place. Thanks to the tour guide at Handunugoda Tea Museum for this lovely experience.
title: Teas and lots of Teas

body: Been to this working tea estate many times over the years and it never disappoints. Well worth the trip out from Galle.
title: Great place to visit near Galle

body: It's nice that everything is in one place. We had excursion around tea plantation and factory, drank tea and bought some in the shop. Prices are lower than in Kandy and other factories in central province.
title: All in one

body: We enjoyed the small roads from our house to the plantation. We were met by Joseph, a local guide, who spend lot of time explaining the tea processing. We had a wonderful tour across one part of the plantation. We enjoyed very much the offered tea and the chocolate cake!!The factory and old machines visit were quiet informative as well.The downside of the visit was the overpriced teas at the plantation shop. We bought few items as a support for the people working there but decided to buy our teas once in Kandy and the mountains area.Nice informative visit for adults and kids but expensive teas if you want to buy some.
title: Beautifull visit but exoensive teas

body: Interesting trip through rural area to reach the plantation, and good views of monkeys as we got out of the coach. Wildlife theme continued with quite a few birds/ a snake and huge variety of plants, many in flower. Informative tour followed by tea and cake, then a visit to the processing rooms followed by the gift shop. Our group all bought some teas having had the opportunity to taste first.
title: Beautiful location, and informative tour

body: Great trip to see a Sri Lankan tea estate. We arrived via tuk tuk and were promptly greeted by a tour guide who showed us the plantation and machinery that was used to make tea. It even included a stop to try some tea and eat some cake. The tour was free but we bought plenty of tea to show our gratitude. Everyone was very friendly and knowledgeable. Would definately recommend.
title: Fantastic tour!

body: Met by a guide on arrival for a walk around the grounds. Explained lots of things and spent a long time taking us to all the machines used for tea making, and to see staff using them Enjoyed that very much including the free tea tasting and chocolate cake! Interesting plantation house where shop is located, but I was very disappointed to see the cost of their tea was far more expensive than standard tea from Sri Lanka in UK supermarkets. Call me cynical but I don't believe that tea produced right in front of you justifies the prices they were charging in the shop to buy. (upwards of £5 a box to nearly £25 a box of their most expensive virgin tea) - Give yourself about 2 hours for a full visit and you don't need to prebook just show up as there are always guides ready to take you around free.
title: Good tour of the grounds, lots of free tea tasting, but tea from shop expensive which is sad.

body: We arrived on scooters, having enjoyed the rural paddy fields and shrines, water buffalo and local communities, to be greeted by wonderfully hospitable guides who showed us rubber trees, cinnamon, teak and mahogany trees, pepper vines and the tea bushes shaded by tall trees to protect their quality leaves.. This was followed by a cup of Oolong tea on the verandah of the century-old plantation estate home and a slice of chocolate cake. Now, that is a welcome!A tour of the tea processing rooms and their machinery exposed us to more old-world charm, with beautiful equipment that is well over 145yrs old and in immaculate condition. To cap it off, their tea-tasting room was a flurry of activity with well over 30 different brews lined up for your choosing.A great experience that connects us with the little black crumbs we take for granted in our morning cups of tea.
title: Serendipity - the Lankan experience

body: Was a great experience, was nice to walk through the estate and see the tea pickers. Friendly informative guides that provide lots of history. The kids got to ride a horse around the estate. We met Mr Herman and had a lovely chat.
title: Nice experience

body: Very informative visit. Warm and friendly guides into a factory with 160 year old still working machinery. Tea tasting was the highlight. Beautiful scenery. Well worth a visit
title: Interesting step back into history

body: Had a wonderful informative tour at my first tea factory. First shown around part of the grounds to see all the different plants (cinnamon, lemongrass, pepper, etc and of course teas). Then had tea and chocolate cake (really good cake) and meet Lara ( 6 month friendly dog). Then got shown around the tea factory and all the machinery. Next stop is to sample all the teas and procure teas, books, cinnamon incense, etc.
title: Very informative

body: It was a great experience for us to visit Handungoda Tea estate.It is a very nice tea estate and a great experience.
title: Great experience

body: Very nice tea estate. You can see 145 years old machines. They offered us their tea and a cake on the terrace of the owners house. Very nice experience.
title: Nice calm experience

body: We took the local bus and then a short tuk tuk ride to get to the tea plantation, and it was really fun. The guided tour was informative, entertaining (thanks Xavier), and free! You get to taste some tasty teas along the way and get a full understanding of the workings of this estate. At the end, there is an opportunity to buy any of their teas, but it is not a situation where you'll feel pressured to make a purchase. It's a nice change of pace from the beach activities. Not sure if it's perfect for kids, but the tour isn't too long, so even if they don't love it, it's over after 30/40 minutes or so.
title: Go here. You won't regret it.

body: Lovely visit , great grounds and our guide was good .tea and cakes served and able to purchase tea.Worth a visit
title: Great visit

body: The tea plantation is the lowest lying tea plantation and the tea grown here offers richer deeper tastes. You need to know where you are going as it is not that easy to find it but it is worth it. The visit does not cost anything but you are expected ( but not obligated or pressured at all ) to leave a tip in the general tip box to be shared among all staff. It is a working plantation so you will see people in action from pickinng silver tips to sorting tea in the drying room. We had the pleasure of being shown how all the machines work - some of them are over 100 years old and in good working order. The pace is unhurried, you can take as much time as you want to stay on the property. There is a lovely tea verandah at the top of the hill - it is the owner's house after all - but they serve tea there to taste in a lovely plantation setting. The tasting room at the end of the tour is impressive and I think there are over 40 teas to try - they have a spitton luckily as otherwise you would end up hyper after trying just a few. While you stroll around the fields, you will see they also grow pepper here and sime rubber trees and it is fascinating to see how teas and spices grow side by side.I highly recommend a visit here. It is equally interesting for adults as for kids.
title: Excellent day at Herman Teas in Handunugoda

body: It is a little bit dificult to arrive there, so i recommend to take a tuk tuk. We found one that took us there and waited for us to finish the tour and took us back for 1200rp. I drink tea every day instead of coffee, but I never knew how diferent types of tea are made, that blac, white and green tea is the same plant! Our guide explained us the whole procedure, from a plant to a cup of tea. On this plantation you can see grow also hibiscus, lemon grass, pepper, coffee... In the end you can taste more than 30 different teas and decide which one you prefer the most. You can taste also the most expensive tea, virgin white tea which is picked very carefully and only 25g per day. The tour is free, but you can give tips in the end.
title: Very interesting, especially for tea lovers

body: Well worth the drive out to the grounds. The grounds are well established, over 100 years old. The gardens are well kept with Hibiscus, roses, rubber trees, mango trees, as well as the tea plants. Our guide was very knowledgeable about the plants and anxious to share his information with us. After a tour of the grounds we had a "spot of tea" and cake at the plantation house before touring the factory. The factory is using equipment set up by the British 150 years ago and still working well. Then on to tea tasting in the gift shop and a look around the museum. Quite an enjoyable experience!
title: Beautiful grounds, interesting tour!

body: It's a bit of a drive but it's quite easy to find with gps or just grab a tuk tuk. The road leading up to it is just amazing, lush fields, small pitoresque villages, truly taken from a postcard. When we got there our guide Anthony was just amazing. He was so knowledgeable and walked us through the gardens to show us the tea and pepper\cinnamon plants\trees. We did tour of the factory as well and some tea tasting. In a country in which they charge tourists for almost anything it was truly amazing to get a tour this good for free! Thank you Anthony!
title: Well worth it!

body: We had a great tour guide who explained the whole process from picking the tea leaves to sampling many varieties. The tour starts with seeing and the guide explaining the tea plants & others like cinnamon and lemongrass. We then enjoyed tea and cake before seeing the factory and the whole process from start to finish. We then tasted so many varieties I lost count. The tour is free but they ask you to tip the lady who serves tea and cake (we left 200 LKR) and there's a donation box split amongst all staff at the end (we tipped 500 LKR). They ask you not to tip individuals
title: Well worth a visit

body: As the plantation is a little way inland you will need private transport or catch a Tuk Tuk from the main coast road (I paid 800Rs return including waiting time, negotiate before travelling)My guide was a lovely friendly man who spoke very good english. He invited me to taste a rare sour grape, turned out to be peppercorns! He was very patient as I took photos and answered my many questions. The tea and cake were delicious, don't forget to leave a tip under the plate for the maid. The factory was fascinating, my mobile phone is 3yrs old and rubbish, these machines are over 100yrs old and still going strong! The tea tasting was amazing, although I felt I needed a glass of water to cleanse my mouth after a few tastes. Be aware that the tea is cold so tastes slightly different. Taste the famously expensive Virgin White Tea and the favourite tipple of HRH Queen Elizabeth (little nod to colonialism)There was no pressure to buy after the tasting but the shop guide was very helpful in selecting a particular tea blend that you will enjoy.
title: Tea heaven, but watch out for the 'sour grapes'! ;)

body: Firstly it's a free guided tour around something genuinely interesting and worth looking at.Secondly from a world of tourism and hustle and bustle which are prominent on the south coast, it's a step in to a bit of calm and quiet.It's obviously quite a "historical colonial" set up, but that period and the tea industry are both very important to the development of modern Sri Lanka.Our guide, an older gentleman was very knowledgable and had a twinkle in his eye. He spoke with knowledge and a genuine interest in the topic. We tried some free tea (the lovely Sapphire Oolong) and cake (Chocolate) before a tour of the still operating factory involving machines over 100 years old.The whole tour maybe takes about an hour and ends in a tasting/purchasing room. Obviously the tour is aimed at a purchase, but there is no hard sell and the product is genuinely worth buying at a reasonable price.I'd highly recommend any tea drinker, lover of history or someone just wanting to unwind to go and treat yourself to a decent brew. Recommended
title: Lovely little detour

body: I visited here as part of a tuk tuk tour with my driver. Kapila. I enjoyed my walk around the plantation with my guide, who I think was called Joseph. I was travelling on my own so was taken round on my own too. Joseph was friendly and interesting. As it was a Poya day, the factory was not actually functioning, but Joseph switched on machines so I could see them in action, and explained what they do.The complimentary tea and cake were nice, although I think the cake was a couple of days old. However it's a nice gesture.The chance to taste several teas in the shop is good, although be aware they are cold. However I didn't find that overly unpleasant. The prices are reasonable for the teas, as they are not your bog standard, mass produced tea bags that you get in the supermarket. As a souvenir I felt the prices were fine, and bought 3 different teas, including a small sample of the Virgin White tea.The tour, tasting and a peruse around the shop took less than an hour so if you are coming a great distance don't expect it to take up half your day. Also there's no set your times. I arrived at about 3pm and there were other tours halfway through and finishing when I got there.
title: Quick but interesting

body: The grounds of the estate are very pretty. Our guide, Anton, seemed genuinely excited about his work which made the tour even more enjoyable. We learned a lot about teas, tasted many different kinds of tea (and yes, the cake), and enjoyed the surroundings.
title: Pleasant few hours

body: first we start walking in the beautiful garden which all the trees have a special story. Then we went in the home to try a tea with a delicious chocolate cake. Then the factory tour, very instructive. The guide took all the time for explaining and answering the question. We finish the tour with tea testing and possibility to buy them. Definitively a must to do.
title: Very special tea visit

body: Entery for free,u can see all the different types of tee trees with a guide,,the tean house hospitaliyy with chai and cake is warm and lovely,,then u can try all the,different typesss of tea as much as u can,,dnt recomend to,buy from there kinda expensive ,,will be nice if u leave tips
title: Lovely

body: Definitely rely vista's here and walk around the plantation with the knowledgeable guides. Rest for a cup of tea and peace of cake at the house then you visit the machinery and see the process.The tea tasting room with around 50 twas to sip was great.Recommended as this is not one of the tea plantations on the major tourist guide route.
title: Peacefully quiet and very informative

body: This is one of the few places in Sri Lanka that we have found that is free. Our tour guide was very informative, spoke very good English and provided us with an insight into how tea is grown, cultivated and turned into the drink we know. You get to experience a good quality tea and homemade cake with only a small donation required. At the end of the tour you can try all of the teas they manufacture, all 30 of them including ones with brandy and vodka! Well worth the visit.
title: Not just for tea lovers!

body: I started by Ahangama town, after 30 minutes reach this place, honestly It was a very lazy day to me with little raining. when I take some tea tastes all the feeling make me happy and I stay there nearby 1.5 hours and take good looking with the tea making process. lots of various of tea you can collect from there. it's a nice place to visit your end of the trip because you can make your love one happy with the gift.
title: Tour make my favorites !

body: We really enjoyed our free private tour through the estate that includes walking throughout the entire plantation, seeing the processing plant where they were actively working to process tea. The tea tasting of ALL of the varieties of tea was awesome!
title: Interesting

body: I hadn't intended to visit this tea estate but went on the suggestion of my tuk tuk driver and it was a real highlight. The tour was very thorough and informative and included a tasting of 65 teas including the rare and valuable white tea.
title: An unexpected delight

body: I visited the Handunugoda tea estate with my daughter today and found the whole experience fabulous. It was the complete opposite of the commercialism of the highland estates where there were tour buses.This estate makes you feel very welcomed, the scenery is beautiful, the pickers looked happy, the tea factory tour is educational, and the tea & cake at the bungalow followed by tasting of around 25 wonderful teas made it a very memorable experience. We got a tuk tuk for Unawatuna area and it took approx. 40 mins.
title: Fantastic

body: This is the home of Virgin White tea. Years ago that meant that even the pickers of the tea, who wore gloves so no human hand touches the tea, were virgins. That virgin pickers have disappeared, but the method of picking remains the same. It is the most expensive tea, but you get e chance to taste it in there showroom, along with tens of other tea varieties. I am not a tea drinker, so I skimmed over that part, but thoroughly enjoyed the free tour that happened before the tea tasting. We learned a lot about the differences between the various types of teas. We walked with the guide through parts of the estate, with him pointing out various plants as well as the types of tea being grown. There was a stop for tea and cake on a nice porch, which was great. The servers there took the babies and played with them while we enjoyed this stop.We watched how they process tea. It was an enjoyable experienceThis is off the beaten track, but if you like tea or are just interested in the process , it is definetly worth looking for
title: A Tea lovers paridise

body: Although a little hard to find, this is a must to visit. Our tour guide was excellent showing us the different types of tea and collection methods. We also got to see cinnamon,pepper and rubber trees. After a slice of cake and a cup of tea to revive us, we were led to the processing area with machinery that is over a hundred years old!. Then back to taste all their teas. As a bonus we observed a small colorful parade outside the plantation.
title: Excellent tour!

body: Just take a tuk-tuk from downtown Galle and 40min later - after travelling thru some local rural sights - you will reach the Estate. What an excellent visit. The guide makes the visit, explaining all there is to know about growing and producing all sorts of tea, rubber, different woods.... Before sampling a suggested tea and cake. Great to see the ladies also working, to get a real sense of how tough it is. Touring the factory and seeing the production line in action was also a highlight. Free sampling of around 30 different types of tea, and as others have said, no compulsory purchase. But how could you not? After such a great experience. So if you want to learn about tea production in Sri Lanka and you have a couple of hours, make sure you put this on the itinerary. It's not like the bustling tea plantations elsewhere, where coaches are unloading bus loads of tourists. It's local, intimate and a lot of fun too.
title: Compulsory for visitors to Galle

body: My tea drinking habits have been converted since visiting this tea factory. Joseph the guide showed us around the plantation and the factory and this was followed by a free cup of tea and a slice of cake. Then into the factory to see the old machines clanking away sorting the tea. Then a visit to the shop (of course!) for a tea tasting session. No hard sales so not obliged to buy anything, but we did and still drinking it at home as it's much better than some of the better known UK brands! A lovely place to visit, away from the crowds and the traffic and the heat. Would definitely recommend.
title: A cup of tea and a slice of cake - Sri Lankan style

body: Very professional. The guide was very knowledgeable and funny. The tea tasting at the end is perfect. Recommended even if you later visit Nuwara Eliya and other cities with many tea plantations.
title: Must-Go!

body: The tour is well worth it forvthe trip. Nice tea and cake served and working museum tour. Very nice place.
title: Good tea.

body: This is a must do for anyone who travels to the South Province. You have a guided tour around a working tea plantation, with tea and chocolate cake in the planters residence. A quick tour of tea factory and the stop off in the gift shop - where there is little to no pressure to buy.
title: Tea Plantation

body: Very well informed by the guide who told us all about the tea process from start to finish We saw the old machines that grade the tea I tasted all the teas and I brought the ones I liked (Cup of tea and slice of cake when you arrive) very nice touch 🍰
title: Holiday

body: The entrance is FREE! The plantation is really great. They grow tea, coffee, pepper, rubber tree, teak and cinnamon. They give you a guide that walks you through the plantation and tells everything about it. Then the give you delicious cake with their tea. After that they take you to the factory and show you the whole process of tea production. Then you go to the museum, where you can try more than 25 different sorts of tea and buy what you like! Great place! Must see if you come to Shri Lanka
title: Great place! Must see!

body: We visited the museum/factory in March and were inspired by a walk through the plantation, and the story of the guide.Wonderful experience.
title: Excellent tea experience

body: Beautiful setting with knowledgeable staff, to ensure you are in line for tea and cake arrive early as do not offer it half an hour before closing time. There are lots of teas to try and buy and a good explanation by the local guide.
title: Go early for tea and cake

body: The tea plantation is worth a visit! The guides are really nice and really try to tell you the idea of making a good tea. You can see all the plants and products like pepper, cinnamon and tea you normally only buy in plastic bags in the supermarkets. Beside that this place is giving work to a lot of local people. So tip well....
title: Its definitely worth it!

body: More of a museum than a working tea estate, but an interesting story and nice teas, if not a little touristy.
title: Interesting Stop Off

body: Tucked into the hillside, this tea plantation specialises in virgin white tea. A tea that is not touched by hand and uses on the finest tips of the tea leaves. We were taken on a free tour of the plantation by an English speaking guide Joesph, who explained the different picking methods and different plantations from Rubber Gum to Cinnamon. We were then taken for afternoon tea on the terrace with a slice of cake and a cup of tea. Back at the shop you can try a sample of all of the teas (cold). The shop was a little expensive but when you remember you paid nothing for entrance, tour and tea and cake, you appreciate the pricing and the wide selection of teas on offer. Well worth visiting if you are in the area.
title: A lovely way to experience the tea industry

body: This was certainly an experience not to be missed. We were shown around the estate, had a very nice cup of tea and cake, then we were shown around the factory to see how the tea is made (37 different types) and some of the oldest machines that are still working. They don't only grow tea, they grow coffee, Peppercorns and they have rubber trees. To the tasting, there were some very good teas, but also some very expensive teas especially the virgin white tea. But an extremely beautiful place and well recommended.
title: Excellent Tour of the Tea Estate

body: My husband and I visited Handuugoda Tea Estate one afternoon and we learned so much about the art of making tea. The tour was free and our guide walked us through the tea plantation and through the factory while production was in process. As an avid tea lover, this was an enlightening experience. After the tour, we were invited to try the 20+ types of tea that are produced on the premises. All were delicious and we brought several boxes home with us.
title: Enlightening Experience!

body: The Tea Factory is a great and learning experience. At the end of the tour one gets to taste over 40 varieties of tea! And also buy some. Should do.
title: Nice visit! And lots of Tea to taste!

body: A lovely peaceful setting, very interesting tour, delicious complementary tea and cake, a chance to taste over 30 teas and to buy some of our favourites. A must go to place if stay in Galle
title: Such a nice afternoon

body: A great tour of a fantastic small lowland tea plantation, particularly if you do not have the opportunity to visit the tea plantations in the north of the country. Even enjoyed a warm cuppa sitting on the balcony of the plantation homestead despite the fact it was about 35 degrees with 90% humidity. The tour was followed by a tasting session of all the teas on offer including the signature white tea. We were able to wander around the shop and there was certainly no pressure to purchase, although we did. On the recommendation of a fellow tourist I also purchased a copy of the Suicide Club – a virgin tea planter’s journey. The book describes the history of the plantation during the British Raj. An interesting read that compliments the tour of the plantation. Highly recommended by the whole family and a great half day tour from Hikkaduwa in a tuk tuk.
title: Great tour for the whole family
