body: Visited this tea plantation during our stay in Fortress koggala.The guide explained various types of tea .And took us into the factory where tea is manufactured . It is 150 yr old machinery which is still working , it was interesting to understand the whole process.We get to taste different varieties of tea .You can buy them from the store if you like.
title: Good place to understand how tea is manufactured

body: From Galle, it's not too far a journey to get to Handunugoda where entrance is free, the tour is free, the information is free, you get a pre-selected round of tea free (with a little cake). The only thing you pay for is if you want to buy some flavoured tea at the end of your visit.It's fascinating to hear the story behind the golden scissors used by virgins to cut special leaves for the Chinese emperor. And the plantation's ownership through the years throws up another telling tale. The factory uses machines that are 145 years old, and they're in pristine condition. It's hard to imagine the place ever using all modern day machinery in the future. Our guide had a screw loose, definitely, but he was also informative, dad-joke funny, and appeared fluent in Russian (which worked out well for the few "Ruskies" who were there the same time as us. Seeing a tea plantation in action is a must if you're in Sri Lanka. If you're in the area (we visited en route to Tangalle), this place is worth the visit. It's charming, welcoming, and has more personality than many other plantations around.
title: Small with a storied past

body: We hired Driver in SL Tours (see my other review) to take us from the port in Colombo to Handunugoda Tea Estate and Galle, for a long day trip. We had found this estate on Tripadvisor. The excellent reviews proved to be correct. An employee gave us a thorough tour, with included seeing the virgin, white tea plants, black tea, rubber tree (with rubber dripping into a coconut collection shell), cinnamon bark and many flowers. We were given a lovely cup of tea on the porch of the owner's private home and even allowed to see his house, which felt like a trip back into British colonial times. We were then given the chance to taste at least 30-40 different teas. We happily bought a few teas we liked. We also left a tip in the tip box because the tour was terrific and he experience a wonderful memory.
title: Beautiful

body: We spent a lovely couple of hours here today. The tour was very interesting, we saw cinnamon, peppercorns and latex trees, as well as the tea bushes. My daughter particularly enjoyed seeing all the old machinery at work in the factory, and of course the complimentary cake which we were kindly given with our cup of tea! It was great that the tour was free and that, although we did buy some tea at the end, there was no pressure to do so, which was refreshing. I
title: Interesting and informative with enjoyable tasting

body: We visited the tea estate a couple of days ago and it was lovely. Such a peaceful and beautiful setting. It's pretty hot but the walk between each part is short. We didn't have to pay anything and we were treated so well with tea and cake plus tea tasting. It was really informative and we ended up buying lots of different varietiess of tea. It's worth a visit if you fancy doing something a bit different for an hour or two.
title: Lovely way to spend a couple of hours

body: Loved our trip to this small but perfectly formed tea plantation.Very laid back and easy going tour. The staff were knowledgable and very happy to chat and give information. The layout is compact so in the heat there are no long treks between factory, shop and plantation as it is all within a couple of hundred meters of each other.The tasting room and gift shop are cool and airy and there's no hard sell or pressure.The delightful bungalow at the end of the tour where you get free tea and cake is a lovely touch and adds to the whole fleeced sensation of the place.Fascinating, pretty and all well organised. The whole family loved it.
title: Brilliant and interesting

body: I visited the tea estate and really enjoyed it. Upon arrival we were a bit confused as to where we needed to go. We were quickly greeted by a local worker who took us on a tour. Very informative. Given the language barrier, he did an amazing job, just pay a lot of attention. We had a cup of their sapphire oolong which is only made there in the world. The tour is free, however its very hard not to leave without buying anything. Delicious tea
title: Lovely visit

body: We enjoyed the information tour in the plantation. They show the way of making tea and the time-consuming and hard work. Sure you can buy tea afterwards. We bought the Saphire Oloong Tea. Preparing the tea at home it tasted fantastic!
title: Very interesting!

body: Tea factory is "a living museum". You will get a free tour in their factory while people are working there; with very old machines. The tour is gone trough with high speed but no one seemed to mind that we stayed in the factory after the tour. After the tour you can join for a tea tasting and buy different, fresh teas (1000rp/packet).
title: Fascinating but small

body: It´s awesome hidden tea plantation with small factory. Just perfect for those who doesn´t have enough time go to the mountains. They make very nice tea as a Virgin white tea or my favorite lemongrass tea. Local guide from estate will show and explain you everything and after that you can taste more then 20 teas!
title: Beautifull place

body: That's the only tea plantation and factory we visited in Sri Lanka and we were quite happy about it. Only thing to mention is the guy that took us on the tour, he was trying to be helpful but the communication was not easy as he mostly didn't understand our questions. The visit is free, it ends with a tour of the shop, prices are not too bad.
title: A nice tea factory... too bad the person in charge of the visit was not speaking a great english

body: There are many tea factories in Sri Lanka that offer guided tours. This one was special partly because of the incredible commitment of our guide. He led us through the romantic estate and the unique historic tea processing factory as if it were his personal property. And, rare in Sri Lanka, he wouldn't even accept a tip. A real gentleman. The lowland tea at Handunugoda is classy, especially the outrageously rare and expensive virgin white tea. Great place off the beaten track.
title: A gem!

body: Amazing that some of the equipment here dates back 145 years.This is a great way to while away 2 or 3 hours and sample a number of types of tea at the end. Don't miss ir
title: Small, but very interesting

body: Starts off with a walk up a short hill path to a bungalow, stopping to illustrate the various plants and uses on this estate. Leisurely and relaxed, with lovely scenery. At the bungalow a cup of tea or two and some cake with a chance to sit and chat. Our guide was charming and really knowledgeable.Then back down the hill and a tour and explanation of how the tea is sorted and processed followed by the chance to sample around 80 different types. You can buy some if you want, but there is no expectation or hard sell. A brilliant change from most other places who are looking to maximise their take from any tourist.Highly recommend this for all ages.
title: A welcoming place, very charming and informative

body: Best of all the tea tours. Learned about loads of other vegetation from seeing black pepper grow to the finale of tea and cake!
title: So Informative

body: Really good trip, great hospitality, mostly about tea but coffee cinnamon and rubber too... Factory museum remarkable... Machines seen working... Very impressive.... Relaxing tea and cake with other visitors... No pressure to buy despite the visit being free 😄
title: Great visit

body: We visited here based on reviews on TA.The visit and tour is absolutely free.You walk through the plantation and sit for tea and cake and then see the processing plant and then you can taste 30 types of tea and purchase teas if you so choose but there is no pressure to buy a thing.The staff is friendly and knowledgeable. The entire visit is about one hour. This place is also know as the Virgin White Tea Estate.
title: Amazing Little Gem

body: One of the few tea estates in the low land of Sri Lanka - and what a great one!It is easy to find the estate if you stay in the south on the island - we took a tuk-tuk from Mirissa, a 30 minutes drive in very nice surroundings. When we arrived we were met by a great guide - he spoke all the languages of the visitors during our stay! - and he gave us the very interesting history about both the famous Virgin White Tea, the Suicide Club and the tea estate and tea in general.The estate has a great history - make sure to get hold of a copy of the book "The suicide Club - a virgin the planters journey" written by the owner Herman Gunaratne. They sell it in the teashop at the estate.The tour around the estate is all free, it lasted for 1 hour and we were served cake and one of the estates special tea, The Sapphire Oolong. Before tea tasting we visited the factory - one of the machines they still use, was build by the same company that build the Titanic! Many of the machines in use was over 145 years old!It was a perfect way to end the tour with great tea tasting and the opportunity to get some of their great tea to bring back home! The whole visit was relaxed and quite and no pressure to buy in the shop - a visit to this estate is highly recommended!
title: A hidden gem - what a lovely tea estate!

body: Visited this tea estate and enjoyed it,the knowledge of our guide and many languages he spoke simply impressed us,and at no charge for the whole visit.
title: Loved this.

body: Just visited the plantation this morning and it was really interesting. The background story is pretty interesting and guide did a good job of explaining everything we were interested in. Part about how Chinese used gold bowls and scissoirs to cut white tea that was never touched by human hands and only Emperor was allowed to touch it was amazing. Virgin white tea has most antyoxydants in any beverage known and is incredibly healthy. Nowdays they use gloves but it's supposedly the only plantation that still uses this way of picking tea leaves. We were also presented with a cup of Sapphire Oolong tea and slice of cake and later we could taste every one of more than 20 teas they have. Everything was free of charge. During the walk we saw Ficus Elastica (india rubber) tree, cinnamon, hibiscus and several other plants species.We really love tea so it was a great experience overall.
title: Lovely Tea Plantation

body: The history of this plantation is very interesting as is the owner who acted as our guide.It started life some 150 yrs age covering 2200 acres but much was gambled away by an ancestor. It is the closest plantation in Sri Lanka to the sea and the only one producing certified WHITE tea. The machinery is 150 years old ( installed 2nd hand) and some 60 people work the estate. The extensive tea sampling is the best part of the tour, with so many variations on offer to buy.
title: Teatime will never be the same

body: Great little trip out with fantastic choice of tea , we had a tour of the plantation and finished off with a choice of 32 cups of tea.
title: Quaint

body: We were lucky to have the owner of the plantation showing us around. He was not only a fascinating character, but also avery skilled storyteller and an endless source of imformation on his subject. One hour in his company, and all of a sudden I, who normally is more of a coffee-person, am deeply moved by the world of tea. We walked around in the plantation, got to see the machinery and had a tea tasting in the end. All of this was for free, but we ended up buying quit a lot of tea since it was sooo delicious! At all times we were surrounded by exotic smells and friendly people. I recommend this activity. It might be good to bring a sun hat and a bottle of water on the guided tour, since it involves a lot of standing around in the sun listening.... :-) and bring a camera!
title: Amazing

body: We took a tuktuk here not knowing what to expect. As soon as we got there we were greeted. After a couple of minutes some more giests arrived. The owner came outside and introduced himslef. This guy was without a doubt a fountain of information. He told us about his plantation, the growth and handling of tea in a very interesting and funny way. He kept his tour light but answered questions in amazing detail. After a while walking outside we sat down in a cozy house and were served an amazing oolong tea. Continuing to his factory afterwards. The tour ended in his small museum where you could taste all tea's made. The highlight being the virgin white tea, untouched by human hands and cut with golden scissors. I'm not a tea freak. I like tea but am not a worshipper. This was still a highlight on our trip so far. Interesting and a fantastic way to spend some time outdoors and away from the beach! Tour was free of charge. You can purchase tea in the museum after the tour. Easy to get there with a tuktuk from Galle/Unawantuna/Talpe/Koggala.
title: Interesting, fun and beautiful

body: This tour was free of charge, had alot og interesting fact about the estate, and didnt last too long! Just long enough for it to be interesting, and stil long enough to be worth the trip! You get a cuppa and a piece of cake, plus you can taste all their tea before deciding to purchase anything. And best of all, NO presuring to buy anything! You can easily leave without spending a penny there!
title: Great tour

body: In this factory we got our own guide, who told us about all the process. People so kind and ready to share.There is also a very nice buildidng for tourist were You can see an ineresting film. But what is important You can try over 40 kind of tea there! And all that for free. Only pay tuk tuk to get You there (from Unawatuna and back, about 2000 rupies).This is really worth seeing. It's location is among beautiful te plantation. Getting there is an adventure too. Through the small villages, rice fields, jungle and cinnamon gardens.
title: Great experience

body: This was our third tea factory tour during our short stay in Sri Lanka. This tour was the best. They allowed you to sample all 32 teas that they produce. Our tour guide spoke excellent English. We had a private tour. Also, the majority of the plant does not run during the day so you were able to hear the guides explanation of each machine. The factory runs overnight during the cooler hours. There was no pressure to buy their tea and it was not heavily populated with tourists. I believe this is also the only factory in Sri Lanka which produces white tea. There is also no admission charge. The only negative is that it is difficult to find.
title: Wonderful Experience

body: We were extremely lucky to meet the owner who kindly showed us round , he is full of the most amazing and interesting stories about his business ( Sri Lanka is the second highest exporter of tea in the world ) Had a wonderful time many thanks!!
title: Amazing!

body: The road to the tea estate goes through beautiful landscape. This was our first visit to a tea factory. The tea estate and factory were interesting to see. Unfortunately the older gentleman guiding us during the walk through the plantation spoke very little english. In the factory a young guy speaking excellent english luckily took over. We were not so impressed by the taste of the teas.
title: Worth a visit if you are in the area.

body: This tea plantation is in a lovely area and the winding journey to get there is certainly very picturesque.Loved the local homes, vegetation and smiles along the way.The Virgin Tea Plantation was run down with very little effort put into interesting information with regards to the plant itself, stages of growth, picking and processing (even though we know this tea is not processed by machinery). It would have been nice to see the difference of the varied tea varieties and get a thorough tour of where the tea is grown i.e, like vineyards. After all, visitors to this destination must surely love tea or at least have some sort of interest in the product? 100% slack.Items for sale are again tourist driven with no creativity in display.We found the tea tasting bland - I much prefer Twinings Teas - sorry!
title: The journey there was the high light

body: If you get the chance to visit any tea plantation in Sri Lanka you must go to this one and if you have a choice of a guide make sure that you get Herman (the owner). He gives the tour a real sparkle of star dust and gravity!The best part of the tour is when you actually see the ladies in their latex gloves with tiny scissors cutting the Virgin White Tea leaves from the bushes that eventually will become the famous tea, which has the highest anti-oxidant content of any tea in the world! It will make more sense when you hear the story! By the way, don't speak when Herman is speaking and be prepared for several stops for him to light up
title: A surprise and delight

body: Definitely worth a visit if you're in the Koggala area. Very well-organised tour of the plantation and factory (which is more like a working museum). The staff are very friendly and will show you around and then take you to have some Sapphire Oolong tea (exclusive to Handunugoda) and a piece of cake outside in the terrace of the owner's property. Feels very colonial. Lastly you can taste (and then purchase) any of the 31 varieties of teas produced. If you're interested in health properties of the different teas, you can read all about this in a leaflet they give you.
title: Tea tasting at its best

body: Great day out for all ages, you get to see how the tea is processed and how it reaches the form that you see in your everyday tea bag!We were very lucky to have been introduced to the estate by Herman himself who gave us a brief introduction to the way in which the plantation works and a brief history into the tea export system.You get to taste the tea along with a piece of cake, at no charge also. There is a chance to buy the tea at the end and it is all very well priced (bag of white virgin tea being 2500LKR)
title: Beautiful

body: I have visited 3 different tea factories and this one is the best. You are allowed to take photos of anything, your guide is patiently explaining everything, you can touch, smell all the outputs....what can I say?! One word PERFECT!
title: The best

body: Its a nice place to stop by on the way to NE if you're not familiar with tea and the process. The tour guides who show you around do a nice job of it.
title: inters-teaing

body: I’ve visited other tea factories in the hill country and these tours were fairly rushed. But in this estate, a charming older gentleman will be your guide. And he will explain you the ins and outs of the tea making process, no rush at all. After you visited the tea plantation, it is time for tea and cake outside a nice bungalow in a pretty garden. Then the tour continues with the tea factory and finally the tea tasting of 30 different teas ! This tour is completely free, but you can leave a tip for the staff. A tea shop is attached to the estate where you can buy all the different teas. Including the famous Virgin White Tea, the speciality tea of this estate. It is harvested by tea pickers wearing gloves. For every tea you buy, you receive a leaflet of how to drink this particular tea and the health benefits. Recommended.
title: A fine experience

body: This was a gorgeous plantation and factory not to be missed. The highlight was seeing the 150 year old machines still in use and working as well as ever. Very humble tour guides who take the time to explain and answer all questions. A wonderful experience for those interested in high quality tea.
title: Genuine view of tea process

body: We took a tuk tuk from Galle to the plantation which is about an hours journey. Great views along the coast and a chance to see Sri Lankan daily life. We read about the tea plantation in our travel guide and knew that it was on a smaller scale than he larger more commercial ones in the north but this was to it's advantage. It's a very successfully run business but has not lost that personal touch. There is no charge and our guide greeted us in perfect English asking if we would mind sharing our visit with a small group of Russian women. We all started off walking up a slight slope and viewing the spice garden stopping at various plants where our guide then broke into fluent Russian before repeating in English. In total he could speak seven languages and was extremely knowledgable. This combination proved to be extremely entertaining for all of us and a really enjoyable afternoon visit. Barriers came down and we had so many laughs together. After the spice garden we tasted some tea (Sapphire Oolong) which is only manufactured here and cake before taking a walk through the manufacturing plant. Some of the machines were built by the same engineering firm as the Titanic and still working. The visit ends up in the tea tasting and gift shop. Here the full range of teas, over 40 can be sampled and of course bought. Handunugoda is a great find and well worth a visit. Intimate in it's scale, professional in it's presentation and delicious teas. Thoroughly enjoyed our time here.
title: A great cup of tea in a beautiful plantation.

body: We have visited tea plantations before but were persuaded by our driver to come here. A tour of the spice gardens was OK. This was followed by tea and chocolate cake on the plantation bungalows veranda. The interesting part of the visit was the factory - still using 150 year old machines from the British. We finished in the shop where you could taste and buy tea. We didn't buy the virgin tea that the estate is famous for - very expensive but labour intensive.
title: Interesting worth a diversion

body: We went to the tea plantation the 2nd day we were here and we are so glad we did as this was a hidden gem. The plantation is beautiful and the tea and tour guides are great too! We really enjoyed it here and would recommend it to anybody! :)
title: So unexpected

body: The best tea factory in Sri Lanka. The rest of them are soo comercial and need to buy a ticket, which is not expensive but they will gave you just a basic staff about the factory and you will be not allow to take any photo! This lovely tea factory is a family business running by fantastic staff. A fabulouse FREE tea tour inside and out side where you can see from beginning the all process - from bush to bag. First part is outside and on the way to 'home house' nice tour guide tells many interesting news not just about the tea but coffe beans or caoutchouc process as well. There you can read some information book about all tea and they gave you tea and chocolate cake - the best one which you can find in Sri Lanka, because they do not have great chocolate like in Europe. After tea time you will see the all proces in the factory. At the end is there museum/shop where you can taste the all 30 type of tea which they have and buy the best which you like. Really recomend the Saphire Olong Tea which you can find only in Sri Lanka!I been there last year with my another friend too. Atractive and worth trip!
title: The best tea factory in Sri Lanka!

body: A fantastic FREE tea tour inside and out from bush to bag.A friendly guide whose English was good and could answer our questions.Really great seeing the workers using the machinery and all seemed happy & passionate about their work.You even get a free cuppa and nibble of cake...FOR FREE!! And get to try over 30 varieTEAS of tea they make.Only thing is it is a bit out the way from Mirissa (15-20k), so a tuk tuk would be pricey. Do what we did and hire a scooter.Definitely worth a trip and don't forget to donate at the end!
title: Tea-rrific!!

body: Great place, beautiful location. Our Guide was awesome and showed us all the ins and outs of the tea making process and the surrounding area. The little tea house at the top of the hill is stunning, and you can even take home some proper tea in the shop at the end of the tour. Well worth a visit.
title: UnbeLEAFable tea tour!

body: Very nice and peaceful experience with tasting, cake, good information and history.The guide was very calm and nice - had good information about the plantation and loved his job - therefore very funny to be around
title: Perfect half-day experience

body: Visited December 2015, Only cost is if you decide to purchase one of the many teas or knick knacks.Free cup of tea with a slice of cake half way round.The old machinery operated by women and a token native whittling some Cinnamon sticks added to the acme experience.Mostly I thought the costs for the tea were reasonable considering I was in a tourist environment.But Virgin White Tea at almost £35 a box was a bit too much, even if as they say it's picked with gloves on hand , scissors used and even the slightest human contact would make it unworthy, I still felt a liberty being taken :)Still, we purchased the chamomile tea and a cinnamon one, plus a couple of nick nacks :)
title: £35 for a box of tea is a bit harsh.

body: This is a must if you are interested about tea. I'm not talking about your PG Tips or any other household brand of tea I'm talking about tea whether a single varietal or a blend these teas strived for quality and passion.Upon arriving we were escorted around the property and given the low down on white, silver, black and green tea.We could see the rows upon rows of tea plants and the pickers diligently filling their baskets with the leaves.A refreshment break of Oolong on the veranda with some cake oozed of a colonial time of long ago, a pause before moving on to the processing of the tea. The plantation is using machinary and techniques dated from 145 years ago a working museum. After the tour of the processing plant, a tasting of all the teas were offered. You could compare and contrast and buy if desired.I enjoyed the visit and the knowledge of the guides.A worthwhile hour spent.
title: Very interesting visit lots learned.

body: Not only a tea estate but also rubber trees, coffee plants, cinnamon production and more to be seen! If the machines are working it is great to gain insight in the daily routine. There is an old Indian racing horse for the kids to ride around.
title: Tea, rubber, cinnamon and more

body: It's a great place to experience a tea estate, tea factory and tasting if you haven't been to Kandy, NE etc. This one is also unique cos they grow the white tea.. However at the end of the tour n tasting, the tea you can buy is pretty expensive! Overall it's a good learning experience..
title: Good tour, expensive buy

body: i guess we had the best tourguide, speaking 7 languages :-) he showed us the faboulus plantation. it was very interesting and we were able to taste, touch, look and listen. the plantation is extremely well maintained and it's far away from mass tourism handling. it's so interesting to see all the ingredients such as cinnamon and lemon grass growing inbetween the tea. they also show you the whole way from green leaves to ready-to-use tea. at the end you can taste all different teas they offer on the plantation. it's highly recommendable! takes you about 1 hour - perfectly spent time!
title: it was just an amazing tour

body: It was raining on the day we visited the estate and this may have contributed to the slightly rushed pace of the tour.We were greeted, on arrival, by an umbrella wielding guide who then proceeded to whisk us round the outside area. He was very knowledgeable, and pointed out many things of interest, but didn't really give us time to enjoy the sights. Also, at one point he did subtly request a tip. You are specifically requested by management not to tip the guides and to report such behavior. Obviously we didn't report him but was a little disappointing, nonetheless, and something to watch out for.The hot tea and cake part of the tour was lovely. Really great tea, made on site, and served in a beautiful and tranquil seating area, overlooking a gorgeous tropical garden.The factory tour is also reasonably brief but very interesting and impressive. Our guide for this section was also very knowledgeable and proud of the factory. And rightly so-the machinery, still in use and in good condition, is over a hundred years old. It's great seeing the tea making process from start to finish and leads nicely into the tasting session.The tasting session is held in the shop, with a view to trying before you buy. There's a short informative film, and then you're given a clean spoon and glass, a description of all the teas and you're free to taste test as you please. There are over twenty teas to try, including the virgin white tea and the famous 'suicide blend'.The purchasable teas are, understandably, expensive for the most part, however there a few reasonable ones and you aren't made to feel pressured into buying anything.Short but enjoyable tour, and as it's entirely free and quite interesting, I'd definitely recommend if you're in the area.
title: Interesting but rushed

body: I was here with my girlfriend. It was very infromative trip, because we saw how grow tea, cinnamon, black pepper, caoutchouc, papaya, ... We received a good pice of cake and it is possible to buy here some gifts. Of course very good tea too.
title: Tea plantation

body: The ride is very nice from Galle in a tuk tuk to get to the plantation, stopping along the way for a coconut juice and bananas. The tea estate tour was an amazing place to visit, especially for someone like me who had never been on a tea plantation before. We got to see so many types of trees, plants, herb and flowers along the way. We took a short walk to the estate where we were served a cup of tea and has a square of cake. After the tour we were taken to the factory to see the processing of the tea that was fantastic and still being done on machines that are more than 145 years old! The tea store was a bit expensive, but you are allowed to taste more than 30 types of teas that are sold. I would recommend to sneak upstairs to see the great paintings and photographs on the walls and there is a great photo opp from the top floor of the plantation. We very much enjoyed and bought a few teas as well as left a donation.
title: Tea Plantation Tour

body: Wonderful experience of seeing the plantation. They Crow everything there including cinnamon, Black pepper, rubber trees, coffee and many other. It is a truly beautiful place and i enjoyed a great Tour including a beautiful cup of tea and a peace of cake at the tea House on the erstate. The Tour on the factory was really quiet extraordinary as the machines are 145 years old and in perfect working condition. One machine is made by the Company who made the titanic. The tea is extremely good and all are very freshly made. Nice shop allows for great buys and bringing the taste of ceylon back home. Well worth a visit.
title: Wonderful and extraordinarily interesting

body: The Handunugoda Tea Estate is unusual in the area being a tea plantation rather than just a tea factory (most of the plantations are quite a distance away). It is well worth a visit - you will be taken on a short walk through the beautiful plantation and shown not only tea plants but other interesting crops too. The walk takes you to the plantation owners bungalow where you will be served tea and cake on the lovely verandah overlooking the gardens, with beautiful views and echoing to the sound of birdsong. You will also visit the tea factory with its fascinating old machinery and then to the "Tea Museum" where you can taste all sorts of teas and of course purchase some. There is absolutely no pressure to buy though and you are left to peacefully browse. I'm a confirmed coffee drinker and even I thought this was a really charming place to visit - it would have seemed wrong to visit Sri Lanka and not gain some experience of tea - this is the perfect place to do that.
title: Charming and interesting place to visit

body: We visited this Ancient Tea Estate as part of our Resort's City tour. Long drive from where we stayed but totally worth it. Get here before the day gets too hot since there is a nice long walk in the beginning. With this walk there is a lot of history attached.I do not want to spoil your trip so will not give too many details.Also included is a factory visit and then the amazing tea tasting. 10 on 10 for them. Hats off.
title: History, Tea tasting, A nice walk and Lovely People

body: Interesting place to visit if you love ceylon tea. The manager was quite nice to show the process and the history of the place. They serve you with a nice cup of oolong tea and a piece of lovely chocolate cake. After that Mr. Mannikkam takes you to show the process of making tea. Finally visitors get a chance of sipping/tasting more then 20 verities of tea.
title: must visit

body: Great excursion for everybody, you will get tour what you never visited and the infromation from the old guy is also very interesting.I thought that I knew almost everything about tea but this tour fill me up to 100%.Very interesting with so nice people.They are selling to all over the world. Best for me is Saphire Oolong tea and virgin white tea.
title: Tea farm with 140years history

body: The Handunugoda Tea Plantation is about much more than tea.The guides are multi-lingual and able to explain in detail about all aspects of the tea making process, specifically they produce the Virgin tea that uses the very young leaves from the tea plant.You are treated to a detailed demonstration that includes working machines that have been used for over 145 years and are still used daily. The tea and cake are enjoyable plus the tea tasting includes about 30 varieties and you are not rushed or pressured at any stage. Additionally there are rubber trees that are producing rubber extract, Teak and Mahogany trees, cinnamon and lemongrass plants and wonderful flora and fauna to take in as you are guided around.There are teas and related-products to buy in the shop but everything else is free.We took a tuk tuk from Bentota to Handunugoda (Dennis Tours) and it was well worth it. A day out to Handunugoda provides lots of photo opportunities and places to visit en-route and is a lot more fun than a taxi!
title: Tea-rrific!

body: This was, hands down, one of my favourite experiences in Sri Lanka and should note be missed by anyone staying near Galle. Herman, the estate owner was very eloquent and passionate about his small estate and we got a real insight into what makes the best cup of tea. There was no obligation to buy anything, but having tried about 30 of their teas (not just their famous white tea) we purchased a few packets for home. Follow the signs for Virgin White Tea to get there and enjoy.
title: Outstanding visit, a real gem

body: This made an enjoyable and interesting hour or two. We had a brief tour of a small area of the estate, tea and (very nice!) chocolate cake before being shown round the small factory. We learnt much more about the process here than we did at the big Mackwoods estate in Nuwara Eliya. We tasted different tea varieties and made a modest purchase. The teas are quite expensive but there was no pressure to buy. We were based near Galle and driving ourselves round and it was easy to find once we located the right turning. By the way, don't believe all the horror stories about self-driving in Sri Lanka. We has no problems at all, including driving through Kandy and Colombo - the roads were generally good although you do need a good navigator as signs are difficult to spot, and reasonable nerves when surrounded on all sides by tuk tuks.
title: Worth the visit.

body: We were taken to this delightful tea plantation by our Tuk Tuk driver Ajith. This place is amazing. the tour starts with a walk in the tea plantation with an explanation about the teas grown and harvested including the famous virgin white this was really interesting. whilst walking in the peace and quiet Guide of our tour also showed us the various trees and wildlife in the plantation. After a rather tasty cup of tea and some butter cake we were shown the factory and tea making process Amazingly old machinery still in use today. We were then offered the chance to taste twenty yes twenty various teas . You also have the option to purchase the various teas they produce, you can also order for home delivery there is no hard sell or pressure to buy, All they ask is you sign the visitors book or make a voluntary donation. We were both very impressedIain and Joyce
title: Wonderful and informative tour

body: We were escorted around the plantation by an extremely knowledgeable man who shared the process of making tea. We were served tea and cake and had the opportunity to sample all the local teas made at the estate. The staff were extremely friendly and welcoming. As a non tea drinker I was sceptical, however if in the area it is an absolute must visit venue
title: Great Free Tour

body: The drive up is as magical as the place itself. Our tour guide knew everything about the tea, and the herbs they grow in the beautiful gardens. After a nice cup of tea with a lovely treat we left for the factory. After the factory we went into the shop. Really nice as you can taste all the different flavours of tea the have. When we bought some tea, and wanted to tip the tour guide he declined and asked to make a donation in the pot. Which is divided under all the employees. Absolutely worth going to !
title: Great place and no hassle

body: You will get a very interesting tour for free trough the estate and the production of tea. It ends with a tea testing and the opportunity to buy some of the excellent teas, but there is never the feeling that you have to be forced to buy anything.
title: Beautiful tour and excellent tea

body: We enjoyed the Tuk Tuk journey to find this tea plantation from our base in Weligama. The gentleman who toured us around was informative and well paced. We had a complimentary cup of tea (and my husband and the Tuk Tuk driver had cake). The tea tasting of the many types of tea was a highlight. It was free and we purchased some very good quality tea in the shop.
title: Informative and super fun experience

body: We really enjoyed the few hours we spent at this tea estate. It was a good 30 minutes away from Galle and half of it on back roads, but they boast producing the ancient Chinese method of virgin tea meaning it does not ever get handled by human hands and the process is painstakingly careful. I am generally not a tea fan, but the teas I tried were very good with lots of variety. Their famous tea, Suicide Club, has such an interesting history! The tour guide was extremely knowledgable and we learned a ton from him. The machinery that is still used is ancient, but clearly seems to still do the trick!Before our tour (which is all free) we were treated to a free cup of tea and piece of cake in their guest house up the hill. The area is beautiful and they even have a race horse on the premises! I highly recommend this location, but seeing as we never visited any of the main tea plantations in the hill country, I can't compare to visiting those behemoths... we did drive by though.
title: A great tour guide, awesome teas!

body: We hired a car and driver from Columbo for the day and wound our way down the coast to Galle. Only in the country for the day I chose this plantation from trip advisor. The driver hadn't heard of it but rang and eventually after winding through the hills just out of Galle we found it.Basic - it's really a working plantation and visitors seemed a bother on the day we went. But none the less the teas are amazing and great value. It's definitely well worth the effort.
title: Flying Visit - out of the way but worth finding

body: We very much enjoyed the guide showing us around at the tea estate who is a living encyclopaedia and speaks more than 7 languages. If you are in the Galle/Kahanda area, well worth a visit
title: Very informative guide and tea plantation with gorgeous location

body: I've been to a couple tea plantations in Sri Lanka and most just show you the tea factory (how tea is made). At Hangunugoda you visit the different kinds of plants and trees and are taught about various teas. Aside from tea, there is a pepper tree, mango tree and rubber tree which you can scratch to let the sap flow (which is collected for use). As you work your way up a trail seeing all these plants and trees until you reach the main house where you take a rest and try the Sapphire Ceylon tea with a slice of cake - complementary :) I do recommend visiting this tea plantation whole en route to Galle beaches !
title: Best tea plantation

body: We had a lovely tour on the tea estate, the guide was a lovely senior gentleman who could speak more than 7 languages and knew absolutely everything about tea and plants in general. We got complimentary cakes and tea tasting at the end. Left with a bag full of wonderful southern teas! Highly recommended!!
title: Beautiful

body: We thoroughly enjoyed our free tour of the estate, which was very informative. However, the highlight for me was the vast selection of top quality and very tasty teas. If you like tea, you will be spoilt here. I highly recommend the Sapphire Oolong tea - don't leave without buying some. The shop accepts card payments as well as cash.
title: Informative visit, excellent teas!

body: While we were rushed during our visit due to grumpy toddlers, the tea plantation was very nice and what we heard from the tour was very good and informative. We had the owner of the plantation and he was full of interesting stories. The tea store was very well stocked and beautifully displayed with tasters.
title: Great tea experience

body: we spent about 2 hours at the tea estate and had a pleasant time. tour of the plantation is informative and nice to have tea and cake half way through. tour of the small factory was good and nice to see 145 year old machines in use - my wife was happy to see they were made in Belfast. tour ends with the opportunity to taste teas in the shop but there is no hard sell and they also operate a central tip box so all tips are divided equally among the staff which is nice to see.
title: Interesting trip

body: Having read such positive feedback regarding the Tea Estate we were somewhat disappointed at what we found. To be perfectly frank we gained more information from Wikipedia although perhaps we just had a poor guide.(in all events we both found him irritating with his puerile questions). It cost us 1500 Sri Lankan Rupees to visit by Tuk-Tuk from Mirissa South (return) and one positive of this was that we stopped at the Fish Market in Weligama for photos, then the Stilt Fishermen 300 (what a scam-but they waved), saw a mongoose and a large monitor and photos of a Buddhist shrine.Returning to the plantation the restaurant is now closed so no chance of lunch. The level of instruction was mediocre although the cake was OK. The tea (without milk and unsweetened was not to our taste) and it was 'suggested' that we might want to tip the waitress! Finally arriving at the 'factory' again it was difficult to believe that the machinery was actually constantly in daily use, as it wasn't. In fact the Japanese separator patently wasn't. On to the tea tasting and I guess at 68 my taste-buds and those of my wife have retired along with us. We tried a variety of the cold, samples but of 20+ we found none to our liking. In fact my buccal membranes dried up I think from shock. Even the blended teas were awful-just so disappointing but who would ever drink cold, stale tea???? Who drinks tea cold, unsweetened and without milk or lemon? OK, I guess lots do but not us.We left without purchasing anything which seemed to disappoint our guide who had mentioned that their only income comes from selling to visitors and some boutique in France. Not sure I can credit this either.It was free but there was a modicum of pressure to buy.Go by all means but don't raise your hopes too high.
title: Bit of a disappointment

body: This tea plantation was such a fantastically beautiful experience, I cannot recommend it enough. The staff were delightful and extremely passionate about the plantation. The history surrounding Handunugoda Tea Estate is extraordinary and so interesting.You're first taken to the tea house for a cup of speciality tea and a slice of chocolate cake (at no cost), here you sit in the sunshine, admire the views and read about the plantation. Herman, the planation owner made the effort to say hello to us and welcome us which was a lovely touch. David was our tour guide and was passionate and interesting to listen to, he has exceptional english and was happy to answer any questions. He didn't rush us and made sure that everyone (5 of us) was ready to move on before continuing with his explanations. After the tea house we were taken for a walk around the plantation and the factory, it blew my mind. We then ended the tour in the gift shop were you had the opportunity to do some tea tasting and browse the gifts.At no point during the tour were we obliged to make any payment, donation, purchase or tip which was such a nice quality about the whole experience considering you're constantly asked for it wherever you go in Sri Lanka. We bought some sapphire oolong tea and Hermans book "The Suicide Club" (excellent read). I'd 100% recommend visiting here during your stay in Sri Lanka, you will not be disappointed.
title: One of my favourite experiences in Sri Lanka

body: This is a very interesting place to visit and we were lucky to be taken around by the owner who told us that he is also a director of Dilmah Tea Company. It was so interesting listening to his story of how he created and sold the Virgin White tea. We toured the plantation and saw the tea harvesting (although in small volume for us tourists), then we had tea and cake at the top of the plantation in the home and tea room, before heading down to the manufacturing area with its 150 year old machinery clacking away. As others have said, the shope has a wonderful collection of teas for tasting and we bought some nice teas and souvenirs for family at home. A must see attraction in Sri Lanka.
title: Must see and different travel experience

body: We went there in September 2014.It wasn't the high season. We had a personal guide around the plantation and factory. It was very enjoyable and a great way to spend an afternoon. The guide was very polite and pleasant, we were not rushed around, and were never pressured to buy anything. We enjoyed the complementary virgin tea and cakes half way round.We bought different teas. The shop is incredible, with samples of all of the teas to taste. Our favourite was the lemon grass tea mix, and also the silver tips.Highly recommended.
title: Nice day, beautiful walk

body: We were pleased that our tuktuk tour from Galle included this place. We had previously been on a tea trail in the hill country, but this time we were able to visit a lowland plantation. We were met by a guide who told us the story of the Virgin White Tea (nothing to do with Mr. Bransom!) and the fact that the present owner's grandfather had lost 1,000 acres of the estate on the roll of dice.The estate is interesting in the variety of produce involved. We were very interested to see the rubber plantation and the spice plants. Before seeing the old machinery and the museum, we were treated to a cup of tea and a slice of cake. At the museum, we had a chance to taste a whole variety of teas. We treated ourselves to some more teas from the shop.Our guide was very interesting and informative so we really enjoyed the visit. There is no charge for the tour, and you are not obliged to buy anything. There is a box for tips which is well worth contributing to.
title: What an interesting history

body: Not only a tea plantation but also a working museum. We found our visit to the plantation informative and interesting, we were lucky enough to be guided by an amazing local and member of the family run business, Xavier. If your going to take the time to drive to the plantation do it the justice of spending an hour or so to really get an understanding or what takes place there. They not only grow tea, but rubber, cinnamon, pepper and other spices. We visited the tea rooms on top of the hill where the view is superb. It was interesting learning about the production process and the benefits of the different teas. Seeing the antique machinery in action was a marvel and an insight into the heritage and tradition of not only this plantation but tea making in general. The production factory is a working museum, that opens your eyes to the effort, hard work and love that go into creating tea, I now have a new appreciation of every cup I pour!
title: Upholding time honored traditions

body: Could not recommend more highly. We got a personal tour by Xavier of the plantation, which consisted of not only tea but several spices and fruits. Sampled peppercorns right off the plant! Once the outside tour was complete, he showed us around the tea processing facility. Heavy machines from colonial times are still in use. The tour finishes with a tasting of around 50 teas, and an opportunity to purchase. Sri Lanka has quite a few tourist traps - This is not one of them.
title: Fantastic Activity

body: This place is fascinating, made more interesting by the fact that it is a low altitude tea plantation. David, who showed us around, was very interesting and helpful. The fact that we were given tea and cake on the owner's terrace really showed how focussed they were in ensuring visitors had a good visit.The fact that this place is the only one in Sri Lanka to produce white tea is an added bonus and the story behind it is very interesting.The tour of the factory area followed by tea tasting was very informative.Would certainly recommend this place if in the Galle area.
title: Fascinating and friendly

body: Such a lovely experience. Our guide was great and told us many interesting things. Loved seeing all these old machines and trying so many different teas. We didn't feel the pressure to tip or to buy anything (even tough we did ;) Also, the cake was delicious!
title: Lovely experience!

body: Hidden away in a beautiful stretch of green, this plantation showcases all you need to know about tea and tea making. Beautiful old machinery, well maintained and a very hospitable reception. No push, no pressure, just enjoy the tea plantation and the friendly tour. The little tea shop offers beautiful teas, even some you may not have tried before. You can taste each tea at leisure.
title: The best tea experience, great history

body: If you like tea- must see. My girlfriend and I enjoied it a lot. Very nice guide- an old man, talking very very slow, but he's very friendly, and has a grate knowledge not just about tea, but general. Estate is very nice, you can try different types of tea, and Virgin White tea.
title: worth to see

body: Loved the drive to the estate through small winding roads and quaint villages. After parking we walked through the tea estate to the tea museum. The staff received us warmly and a guide took us on a small tour of the estate. He explained everything in a most knowledgeable and friendly way. The guide then took us to the tea estate owner's bungalow where we were given cake and tea, free of charge. We were taken to the tea museum where we watched a film on tea making and tasted different types of tea. There was no pressure to buy anything and the guide refused to accept any tips. We bought some nice cinnamon tea. It was a nice experience overall. Very much recommended.
title: Great experience!!

body: We went here one day as part of a day trip to Galle. On arrival, we were promptly introduced to the owner of the Estate and then a guide took us through a small section of the plantation and up to the owner's house. On the way he explained the various types of produce they grow including tea, coffee, and rubber. At the house we were offered some cake and tea. The history of the tea estate is fascinating - refer "The Suicide Club". Afterwards, we were shown through the factory where tea is manufactured by some old but fully functional machinery, which was very interesting.We finished at the small shop where we tasted some tea and bought some of their specialties. TIPS:- There is no entrance fee. The tour is free.- There is no expectation that you tip or purchase any of their products. - The tour takes about an hour. - Wear a hat and take some water. Walking through the plantation is hot work!
title: So that's how tea is made! - note my TIPS!

body: Had a fascinating tour of the estate and tea production area. Tea tasting afterwards was amazing too.
title: Beautiful Tea Estate

body: We visited this tea estate by tuk tuk from unawatuna.It's free and you have a guide to show you around. First we had tea and cake in the owners house which was lovely, the setting is picture perfect.Afterward we looked at the tea, coffee, cinammon, rubber and lemon grass plantations just to name a few. From here we looked at the drying, rolling and sorting process which was really cool. They have 150 year old machinery that was built by the same company that built the Titanic.At the end you get to taste all of the teas and purchase if you wish.The only problem I have with this place is that after we did not tip our guide his face changed and was suddenly not so friendly. However after buying 20,000 Rs worth of tea I'm sure his commission cut would have been enough without the tip.
title: Nice informative hour

body: The place offers free tours in a local tea estate and its a really nice tour indeed. They don't force you into buying anything and don't ask for tips, but the whole thing is formed very intelligently in a way that makes you want to buy something from them and then you pay the bill. You will want to buy something because you really enjoy the tour and thats OK, but the thing is that they charge very high prices for the tea they are selling. Especially the expensive White Tea, which they promote from the moment you arrive.Don't get me wrong, they are not doing anything bad. They are just offering a premium shopping experience for premium prices and I'm writing this review so you'll be aware of it. My recommendation is: Go there, enjoy the tour and buy one or two packages of tea as a gratitude. Don't buy the really overpriced White Tea and don't buy large quantities. Really good tea grows in the mountains and therefor their tea is not of the best quality you can find in Sri Lanka.
title: Great business school - Nice tea estate

body: I've visited other tea plantations where you have to pay for the tour and they offer only a cup of tea.Not here. You get a tour of the estate, a guide who explains and shows you the tea processing from the beginning to the final product and, the best thing, you taste all types of tea, for free. Yes, and if you don't want to buy tea it's fine, nobody is going to push you into purchases.If you want to visit a tea factory this is the best deal. Go to Nuwara Elia only for charming pictures in tea plantations but do not go for a paid tour, you'll get a lot more here.
title: Informative, free and worthy

body: On a rainy day took a tuk tuk from Unawatuna to check out the estate. Free tour that shows 150 year old British machinery at work. Followed by a tour of the owners house with a free cake and tea! Woohooo!!! And finally a tasting of all the teas they produce. You are not pressured into buying anything but the tea was great and I picked up some tea. definitely worth a visit.
title: Amazing!!!

body: This was one of the best things we did in Sri Lanka. You become used to being constantly hassled and cajoled into parting with your money, so to visit somewhere so peaceful and beautiful, and to be given it for free, with no obligation to buy anything, is a unique experience. The tour is very interesting, giving you a real understanding of the process of making tea. The free tea and cake on the veranda is shady and restful. There is a shop with dozens of free samples you can try. We didn't buy anything and there was no pressure to do so. A thoroughly enjoyable and commendable trip out.
title: Paradise

body: Travelling between Galle and Tangalla, we made a diversion to this wonderful tea estate, and were taken under the very broad wing of Mr David, the General Manager. He gave us a comprehensive tour of the area around the factory, and then the factory itself. On the way, we were given some Oolong tea and home-made chocolate cake, while Mr David proudly told us everything there is to know about tea, and most especially about the estate's pure virgin white tea: reputed to be highest of all teas in antioxidants. He answered all of our questions generously and thoroughly, and was courteous and extremely welcoming. We left feeling refreshed, better informed, and totally charmed.
title: A delightful side-trip

body: We took a tuktuk from Unawatuna to visit the Handunugoda Tea Estate, and if memory serves me well, it took about 30 minutes to get there. Our tour was given by a clever and very knowledgeable man named, Xavier, who was extremely interesting and good fun. We not only learned about the very special "Virgin White Tea", but about other types of tea, cinnamon bark, rubber trees and pepper production. We were treated to a lovely cup of tea and chocolate cake in a most beautiful garden setting. We were given a tour of the factory where we learned about the drying, cutting, sorting and grading of the tea. And, when the tour is finished you can sample one or all of their teas and purchase them if you like. There is absolutely no pressure to buy. We did not see anything advertising the tea estate tours, but happened upon a review here on tripadvisor and we are so glad that we did. It really was one of the highlights of our trip to SriLanka. Later in our trip we visited and toured the large Mackwoods Tea Plantation. The tour there was nothing at all like the one at Handunugoda. Mackwoods is a gigantic producer that sells to brokers at auction. The tour itself is very short and impersonal. Handunugoda is a small operation and a labor of love, and it shows. And , if you are advised by anyone outside of the tea estate not to buy the tea, don't listen. If you are inclined to buy it, buy it. You will not likely have the chance to purchase this tea anywhere else later on, and you will have wished that you did. It is lovely tea.
title: Well worth the trip!

body: This was one of my favorite activities on our journey. The tour is thorough and free. It includes the plantation and factory. You get a cup of tea and bit of cake halfway through. Rubber trees, a variety of teas and black pepper are just a few of the items grown here. The tasting room was fantastic. There was no pressure to buy (though I did buy a lot because it was all so good!) and a sign is posted asking you not to tip your tour guide but to put funds in a general bin if you liked your tour. They don't use pesticides so there are a lot of red ants about, watch for them, just keep moving and you will be fine. Find them online at http://www.virginwhitetea.com/
title: Wonderful!

body: The tour was very relaxed and nice. You can try all types of tea and have a relaxing ceremony and talks about the history of the plantation. Then you can can come to the production area and see all the stages of the tea preparation. David does a great job explaining everything in a very interesting manner.
title: Recommended!

body: We had a delightful visit here. We learned so much from our host David. We sampled over 20 types of tea and began to appreciate the differences in harvesting and production. Watching gloved women harvest the delicate Virgin White Tea was an experience. The gardens and grounds on the plantation make for great stroll. A surprise for us was seeing the processing of the tea using antique machines, themselves works of art
title: beautiful tea plantation

body: perfect add-on to other tours in the area. We combined our visit with a beach trip to Mirissa. Short enough not to bore our 8-year old son. Horse ride also available but we didn't opt for it in the end. Interesting and well-presented introduction to the process of making the virgin white tea and the other varieties of black and green tea, and of course a tasting at the end. Try the Suicide Blend! Nice gifts to purchase in the shop after sampling the numerous tea varieties. Lovely spot for photos. Feel lucky to have found this excursion which we found easily manageable by road from our base in Unawatuna.
title: great tea plantation visit without the long drive to the hills!

body: I'll have to agree with all the other people who speak so highly of this little excursion! No obligation to buy, no suggestion even to leave a tip in the tip box (but if you enjoy the tour and tasting as much as we did, it seems normal to leave a little something for the friendly and informative staff) One piece of advice - if you have the slightest interest in the history of tea or information about this plantation's evolution, call ahead to ask for "Herman" (the owner) to take you around. The 'normal' guides were great, but Herman was had some awesome anecdotes and insight.
title: Very enjoyable, informative and beautiful!

body: We enjoyed the trip to the tea plantation near Unawatuna, about 10 minutes by car from the beach. Free you can visit the factory processing of tea. The visit is accompanied by an engaging lecture with demonstration of tea processing. In conclusion, visitors can taste about 20 types of tea. Highly recommended.
title: Taste of tea on your trip

body: I'm not a particularly big tea drinker but I was curious to see a plantation and my girlfriend really wanted to buy some good Ceylon teas whilst we were visiting. It is quite a way from the main roads, but when we arrived we were met by a guide (Xavier) who first showed us the various tea leaves and rubber trees, before taking us up to a bungalow on the hill, where we were served some cake and a cup of their own tea.Following this we walked down to the factory buildings, where we saw the entire process from drying the fresh leaves to bagging the finished products for shipping. At no point was money/tipping mentioned, which was a refreshing change from other attractions we had been to in Sri Lanka. When the factory tour was over it was suggested that we have a look in the shop, where we could buy the different varieties of teas they produce. All the different flavours were laid out for you to try, and we left with a few boxes of not inexpensive (about the same price as good quality tea in a US/European supermarket) teas. Others who didn't wish to buy anything were allowed to leave without hassle.All in all it's well worth a visit. It is an interesting and well explained tour of the tea making process, and it was nice to be allowed to wander at your leisure without being given a hard sell. Plus, if you like tea, they have an endless list of varieties and all of it produced on the estate.
title: Well worth a visit

body: Peaceful and no pressure to buy like most tea plantations in Sri Lanka. It is in the south not far from Galle and no where near the traditional tea areas visited by tourists. The owner is an author and has written a book The Suicide Club, a book about the heydays of tea production in Sri Lanka. Highly recommend a visit.
title: Best Tea plantation in Sri Lanka

body: Don't miss this excellent free tour with chance to sample and buy the tea at the end. You get to see the tea and rubber plantation the the leaf drying and tea making processes followed by a chance to sample the products and make a purchase.
title: Well worth a vist.

body: Really great tour, explaining the tea making process from a to z, possibility to taste many kind of teas. Recommended for everyone.
title: Great tour

body: Went to a couple tea plantations / factories in Sri Lanka - this one was definitely a highlight. Appreciated the time the staff took to explain the production process and also to sample the teas (approx 20 teas), including complimentary cake. Highly recommend.
title: Authentic non touristy feel, detailed explanation, little to no pressure to buy, phenomenal tea

body: for the first time hear about virgin tea, as the guide explain they cut the first un open leaves by not touching it. so as he explain until end of the processes those leaves are not touch by human hands. guide explained lots of things about flora in the garden, also he show us black monkey at the first time we saw in sri lanka. after had a tea at the house on top corner of the garden, then experienced of a great factory explanation about the machines they have used. it is excellent.after taste all type of teas they have we can decide what we need. that is a great service which we didn't see in other tea factory we visit on the way to nuwara eliya.
title: Excellent tea plantation visit

body: We visited this tea plantation with kids age 5 upwards and all of us enjoyed the tour.It was hidden away and we drove through the beautiful Sri Lanka countryside to reach it. The guide managed to keep the children interested all the way around. Our kids were particularly interested in the rubber tree and how they harvested it. The guide then gave us tea and cakes at the plantation owners house. it was like stepping back in time. The factory and museum were all equally fascinating and it was great to taste all the teas at the end.
title: Informative trip for all ages

body: After a series of twists and turns along pot-holed roads we reached The Virgin White Tea Plantation, a beacon of serenity. Our guide was an extremely knowledgeable older gentleman whose passion for the flora and fauna was infectious. We were shown plants of coffee alongside white and black tea, peppercorns, trees of mangoes, jackfruit, cinammon, teak, mahogany and rubber. A live demonstration of the latex sap collection was fantastic. This part of the tour was followed by an equally as long tea and cake break, soundtracked with the history of the estate owners. Later we had a tour of the working factory to see the tea being produced. The tour ended with a tasting room filled with the 27 teas, there was absolutely no pressure to purchase anything. Small bags of tea were priced around 700RPS. I can't believe they do not charge for this tour, that there is no hard sell and that the staff are so happy to talk about tea. This place is a real gem; the practically overflowing tip box is testament to this.
title: Refreshly relaxed, educational and honest

body: We had a superb tour of the estate, factory and tasting room. It's a very peaceful, professional yet authentic place. Our guide, Mahendra, was very knowledgable and we thoroughly enjoyed the visit!
title: Excellent Tour!

body: A large group of us ranging from 2 to 50 years old visited the Handunugoda Tea Estate a few weeks ago. We had a great afternoon being shown around the estate, drinking tea and eating cake up on the hill, admiring the owner's former race horse and all the classic original giant British machinery still churning reliably away in the factory before descending to the tea museum where we sampled - and my wife went on to buy - practically every tea under the sun, as well as a colourful range of historic Ceylon postcards and posters. This is a serene and informative place, quite a winding road to get to it but one of the best outings in the South of Sri Lanka without a doubt. Highly recommended.
title: Very educational and inspiring re. tea's detoxifying properties!

body: We were a bit sceptical when our Tuk-Tuk driver suggested this place but as we were able to trust him agreed that we should go. So glad we did. We had one of our best trips in all our holiday. We were very lucky to be shown around by the owner Herman and as we were not part of a group we felt very privileged. We could have listened to this gentleman for hours. His passion was tea but had a full repertoire of interesting and amusing anecdotes. We had tea and chocolate cake on his veranda and were taken on a very interesting tour of the plantation and factory.The tasting room was very good but at no time were we pushed to buy any tea, and after wards were left to decide whether we would buy or not . We did. A great day out and FREE, a sad rarity in Sri Lanka.
title: Great place and its free

body: I'm really pleased we took the time to visit this Virgin White Tea plantation. It was in a beautifully scenic location and we started with a free guided tour. It was so interesting, really informative and educational. The children loved it and had lots of questions. It was really intriguing to see the old machinery, which they still use, made by the same company that supplied parts for the Titanic! We then went for tea tasting, which we all loved, and decided on a few purchases of some exceptional teas that were new to us! The whole visit was very enlightening and pleasurable and the friendly people at the plantation make it a must-do excursion!
title: Wonderful afternoon!

body: This plantation is completely free to visit, we had a very interesting tour of the plantation, working factory and museum. Beautiful tea and cake in the picturesque surroundings up at the plantation bungalow which was free whilst we learned the benefits of various teas. we brought lots of tea to bring home but it was one of the few places that we visited where there really was no pressure to buy anything. Well worth a visit!
title: Tea plantation

body: I've been to many tea estates but to date this has been the pick especially with Herman Gunaratne as an enthusiastic & entertaining raconteur. The estate is scenically positioned in the low country & the process well explained including a short break for tea before visiting the factory, a tea tasting and opportunity to purchase not just tea but one of Herman's entertaining books. The whole visit is very well done & is great fun.
title: A fun visit - well explained and fun. Highly recommended

body: We have really enjoyed our visit at Handunugoda Tea Estate. These people really do what's their passion, they make excellent tea and take good care of the visitors. It's interesting to see how the tea is grown and processed. The cake & tasting was a nice surprise...I'm enjoying the teas from this tea estate now back in the office :) I would say for us this was the most enjoyable attraction in Sri Lanka.
title: Must see if you like Tea

body: We had a great visit to the tea factory & plantation, much thanks to our great guide. Good place to learn more about tea and its history. Take money with you so you can buy the excellent teas from their teashop.
title: Must see in southern Sri Lanka

body: Fantastic place! It was a great experience to be able to see a tea plantation. Fantastic photography opportunity as well. People as typical for Srilanka very friendly. There also are couple of cinnamon peelers over there to give you an idea how cinnamon is harvested. Beautiful experience!
title: Fantastic place!

body: One of our friends in Sri Lanka suggested visiting the Handunugoda Tea Estate, and we followed his suggestion. We were greeted by The General Manager of the Property Mr. David Manickam, who gave us unforgettable tour of the plantation, explained how they cultivate the famous Virgin White Tea, how the tea is produced, packaged, etc. The cup of Sapphire Oolong and then a Rainforest tea accompanied by the delicious homemade chocolate cake was the delightful break during the hot day. Then we visited the museum and tasted all teas produced in the Estate, including the Virgin White Tea. What an experience! The visit to the Tea Estate can’t be completed without the purchase of the Virgin White Tea! Don’t miss the opportunity to visit the Handunugoda Tea Estate! It is free learning experience!
title: What an experience!

body: This tea factory is located in the South-West of Sri Lanka near Galle. Ask a TukTuk driver to take you there. Either select a vehicle with taxameter or one of a licensed driver. This can be identified by a corresponding license number on the windscreen. Both assure, that you pay for each driven km and not for the fantasie of the driver. Our driver knew the Tea Estate were allowed to be our guide. He brought us to the owner's house, where we got a piece of cake and two cups of tea, one without and one with cinnamon.The driver showed us green pepper, cinnamon and - needless to say - the tea bushes, a small factory and the tasting house, where we could taste about 20 different teas.
title: Learn more about tea and taste some varietes

body: A meander through the plantation, complimentary refreshments on the veranda of the bungalow, a tour of the working tea factory, then tea tasting and shopping (with no pressure to buy). A fascinating insight into the tea industry and the world famous virgin white tea.If you only have time to visit one tea plantation then Handunugoda is probably the best there is.
title: Simply the best

body: My boyfriend and I visited the tea plantation yesterday and we have nothing but positive comments about the experience. I needed the toilet as soon as I arrived and was surprised at how clean and modern itwas. So many public toilets are disgusting in Sri Lanka so to see a clean one was lovely.David our guide was so informative and despite the fact that I'm the tea drinker in my relationship I think my boyfriend enjoyed it more than I did. He doesn't drink tea but David answered all his questions about production and general state and ownership of tea production in Sri Lanka.We walked past Herman the owner of the plantation which was exciting and he's equally friendly. We were shown the speciality teas, the rubber trees which originate in Brazil, machinery which was over 150 years old still being used and finally we had tea and yummy chocolate cake.I must add here that there is no entrance fee and you are given the choice to taste about 20 different teas and choose what you want to buy and take home. We spent a small fortune on tea (20,000 rupees) out of personal choice and the people in the shop were able to tell me the ones with the best health benefits. This is truly a must visit if you are in the area.
title: Fantastic tea plantation

body: It was an interesting place but I have to say that comparing the prices for the same products in Galle it was more expensive. For example the same poster I saw in Galle was priced at 2500 Rp at a boutique shop as opposed to 3000 Rp at the tea place. Maybe there are some commissions at work here since the tour is 'free'.
title: Interesting but overpriced gift shop

body: I would have never thought that a visit to a tea plantation can be so interesting. I really enjoyed my visit there.The tea factory itself is, as written on a plate, is a working, living museum. I was fascinated by the old machines (over 145 years old!), and the whole process was described with lots of details by the guide (Chris?). After a week, I visited another tea plantation, so I could see the difference. The experience at Handunugoda Tea Estate was much better.Beside the museum-like factory (that was similar to the other one I have seen), here I have also visited the plantation, I have been shown different types of trees and plants (rubber tree, mahogany, ebony, bread tree, sugar cane, pepper...), and I also had two complimentary cups of tea and a cake on a very nice porch. Also, the tea shop was very nice: 27 types of tea to taste and/or buy.Very pleasant and interesting visit!
title: Very interesting

body: After visiting three other plantations in the hill country we were not sure that we wanted to visit a fourth but are so glad we did as this was the best. The guide was excellent in his explanations of the teas, the birds and the rubber trees and the cinnamon trees. Then we had two different teas and chocolate cake on the verandah of the lovely home facing the gardens. The tea factory was very interesting especially with its antique machines all so beautifully restored and working. The tea tasting was a great experience and we ended up buying some teas which we are enjoying now at home. We cannot buy tea here in Canada that tastes like this tea. The whole thing was delightful and we would go back again in ever in Sri Lanka. The tour was free unlike some other tea factories in the hill country. All in all well worth a visit.
title: The Best Tea Plantation we Visited in Sri Lanka

body: My driver randomly took me here, and I could have stayed all day! The guide was extremely informative, the plantation has a wonderful history. Ask any question and they will know the answer. Watching the tea being produced was really interesting, and the tea-tasting experience was wonderful. For a 1-2 hour change of pace, I 100% recommend this place.
title: Highly recommend!

body: This place didn't appear in my guidebooks but it popped up on a website about Koggala where I was staying. I'd previously had a negative experience of a tea estate in the highlands, much too touristy, so this estate was a breath of fresh air - literally, with the stunning scenery! The guide who took us round spoke excellent English and explained the history of the plantation with interesting anecdotes about the owner's family. After looking at the growing tea, we went to the owner's colonial-style elegant bungalow for a very polite tea and cake on the terrace, facing lovely gardens and a beautiful view.. This was followed by a visit to the factory, not actually working at the time unfortunately, but everything was well explained and it was fascinating to see the very old machinery, still in use. The tour ended in a beautifully arranged shop/museum, where we had a chance to taste 24 different teas! These were all on sale but the prices put me off, although the rarity of this type of tea made it well worth buying for conoisseurs. The whole experience lasted nearly 2 hours, yet was absolutely free! There was a box for donations, but no demands for payment at all. I would definitely recommend Hanungoda as an attraction worth visiting, even if you are staying quite a distance away, as it was so different from other money-seeking attractions I've visited.
title: Great experience.

body: This place, hidden inland of Galle, is a place you must see! It is the only tea estate that close to the beach and produces the famous white virgin tea. The owner is the author of the well known book ' The suicide club' and the suicide blend is also available with a hint of whiskey. Very friendly and welcoming guides will show you around. The fabric is fascinating with its old machines (made by the same manufacturer as the Titanic). At the end you will have a tea tasting which is lovely!
title: Worth well visiting!

body: Stumbled upon this place by chance after reading a tiny note about it in a guide book. We have visited the the plantations of the highlands and although the views and quantity of tea here are not as jaw dropping, the actual tour itself puts Hapatules tea factory to shame.
